entries.title: a nonempty transporter is a bitorsor
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: If a group G acts on X and g₀x=y, then the transporter T(x,y) equals g₀Gₓ=Gᵧg₀; its right Gₓ and left Gᵧ actions are free and transitive, and Gᵧ=g₀Gₓg₀⁻¹.

entries.title: kernel-orbit refinement is an exact coset space
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Let φ:G→D be a surjective group homomorphism, K=ker φ, and H=Gₓ. The K-orbits inside Gx are naturally in bijection with the left cosets D/φ(H), by K·(gx)↦φ(g)φ(H).

entries.title: correcting a supplied transporter
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Under A002, if gx=y, a K-transporter exists exactly when φ(g)∈φ(Gₓ). If h∈Gₓ has φ(h)=φ(g), then gh⁻¹ is such a transporter.

entries.title: exact stabilizer sequence and fibre size
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Restriction of φ gives an exact sequence 1→K∩Gₓ→Gₓ→φ(Gₓ)→1. Each nonempty character fibre in Gₓ is a coset of K∩Gₓ. For finite Gₓ, |Gₓ|=|K∩Gₓ||φ(Gₓ)|.

entries.title: orbit-count multiplication under refinement
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Assume G and D are finite in A002. Then Gx contains exactly [D:φ(Gₓ)] K-orbits, and each has size |K|/|K∩Gₓ|.

entries.title: sufficient fibrewise orbit recovery
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Let f:X→Y be G-equivariant. If each nonempty fibre f⁻¹(y) is transitive under Gᵧ, then two points of X are G-equivalent exactly when their images are G-equivalent.

entries.title: pairs of orbit points are classified by double cosets
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: For stabilizers H=Gₓ and J=Gᵧ, diagonal G-orbits on Gx×Gy correspond to double cosets H\G/J. The pair (x,gy) has stabilizer H∩gJg⁻¹.

entries.title: character images survive unipotent splitting
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Suppose G=U⋊L and a homomorphism χ:G→D is trivial on U. Then χ(G)=χ(L). More generally, for a subgroup S≤G whose projection to L is S₀ and which contains U, χ(S)=χ(S₀).

entries.title: abelian stabilizer characters are orbit invariants
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: Let D be abelian and φ:G→D a homomorphism. If x,y lie in one G-orbit, then φ(Gₓ)=φ(Gᵧ). In particular the determinant image of a tensor stabilizer is unchanged by an invertible tensor transporter.

entries.title: a uniform fixed-field determinant-automorphism compiler
entries.section: I. Transporters, stabilizers, and exact orbit information
entries.statement: For each fixed finite field F_q there are polynomial-size, uniformly constructed pairs of ordinary three-tensors C(A,d),D(A,d) such that C(A,d)≅D(A,d) exactly when A admits an automorphism with determinant triple d∈(F_q*)³. The polynomial bound is in the number of entries of A; no transporter is supplied.

entries.title: intrinsic mode supports are the minimal tensor carriers
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: For t∈U⊗V⊗W, let S_U be the span of all contractions (id⊗β⊗γ)t. Define S_V,S_W similarly. Then t∈S_U⊗S_V⊗S_W, and every carrier U′⊗V′⊗W′ containingt has S_U⊆U′, S_V⊆V′, S_W⊆W′.

entries.title: transporters restrict to concise cores
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: If (P,Q,R)t=t′ with all three maps invertible, then P(S_U(t))=S_U(t′), and similarly in the other modes. Conversely an isomorphism of the three supported tensors extends to an ambient transporter whenever the corresponding ambient dimensions agree.

entries.title: zero padding turns GL-equivalence into SL-equivalence
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: Add one zero coordinate in each mode of two tensors of the same dimensions. The padded tensors are equivalent under special-linear maps exactly when the original tensors are equivalent under general-linear maps, over every field.

entries.title: rank-one stabilizers and free determinant coordinates
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: A nonzero decomposable tensor u⊗v⊗w has stabilizer consisting of triples preserving the three factor lines, with line multipliers a,b,c satisfyingabc=1. If each ambient dimension is at least two, its determinant image is all(K*)³.

entries.title: flattening ranks give independent tensor invariants
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: The first flattening of t is the linear map U*→V⊗W induced by contraction. Its rank equals dim S_U(t), and invertible changes in all modes preserve this rank.

entries.title: tensor products multiply mode ranks
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: For tensors t and s over K, the first-mode flattening rank of t⊗s, with corresponding modes grouped together, is the product of their first-mode ranks. The same holds in the other modes.

entries.title: tensor rank is unchanged by injective ambient padding
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: Injective linear maps in the three factors preserve the tensor rank of a tensor. Thus zero extension does not create a shorter decomposition into pure tensors.

entries.title: recovering a bilinear map from its radical algebra
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: Let β:V×V→W be symmetric, have image spanning W, and satisfy {v:β(v,V)=0}=0. Define A=K⊕V⊕W with identity1, product vv′=β(v,v′), and W(V⊕W)=0. Algebra isomorphisms between two such algebras induce equivalences of their β maps.

entries.title: isotopy of unital associative algebras normalizes to isomorphism
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: For unital associative K-algebras A,B, suppose invertible linear F,G,H:A→B satisfy H(xy)=F(x)G(y). Then A and B are isomorphic as unital K-algebras.

entries.title: centroid idempotents split a bilinear tensor intrinsically
entries.section: II. Tensor supports, faithful restriction, and algebra recovery
entries.statement: Let β:U×V→W be bilinear. Suppose idempotents e_U,e_V,e_W satisfy β(e_Uu,v)=e_Wβ(u,v)=β(u,e_Vv). Then β is the direct sum of its restrictions to the image triples and the kernel triples; all cross terms vanish.

entries.title: subgroups of a finite-rank free abelian group are free
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: Every subgroup L≤Z^r has a basis of at most r integer vectors.

entries.title: Smith normal form by decreasing Euclidean pivots
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: An integer matrix M can be transformed by unimodular row and column operations into diag(d₁,…,d_s,0), with each d_i>0 and d_i dividingd_{i+1}.

entries.title: monomial equations reduce to independent power fibres
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: For an abelian group H and integer matrix M, define f_M:H^s→H^r by (f_M(x))_i=∏_j x_j^{M_ij}. Smith operations turn f_M(x)=a into independent equations y_i^{d_i}=b_i and equations b_i=1 for zero rows.

entries.title: two simultaneous powers have one residual root
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: Let H be abelian, d,M,N integers, and Mr+Ns=1. Then t^{dM}=a and t^{dN}=b are simultaneously solvable exactly when a^N=b^M and a^r b^s has a d-th root in H.

entries.title: finite cyclic monomial fibres have exact sizes
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: IfH is cyclic of orderm, then x↦x^d has kernel sizeg=gcd(m,d), image size m/g, and a belongs to its image exactly when a^{m/g}=1. A nonempty Smith-system fibre therefore has size m^{s−rank M}∏_i gcd(m,d_i).

entries.title: a subgroup of(C_m)^r is cut out by r characters
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: Every subgroup S≤D=(Z/mZ)^r is the simultaneous kernel of at most r homomorphisms D→Z/mZ.

entries.title: finite character sums are exact subgroup projectors
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: Let K contain a primitive m-th root ζ and assume char K does not dividem. For S≤D=(Z/mZ)^r, average all characters trivial on S. The resulting function is1 on S and 0 outside S.

entries.title: scalar kernels constrain semi-invariant degrees
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: Over an infinite field, let a nonzero homogeneous polynomialf of degree d on U₁⊗⋯⊗U_s satisfy f((g_i)t)=∏det(g_i)^{a_i}f(t), with integersa_i≥0. Then d=(dim U_i)a_i for every i.

entries.title: finite-field determinant images admit three bounded equations
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: For a tensor over F_q, its stabilizer determinant image Δ≤(F_q*)³ is described by three monomial equations with a3×3 exponent matrix whose entries lie in[0,q−2].

entries.title: intrinsic extraction of a bounded determinant equation table
entries.section: III. Integer lattices, torus characters, and exact power equations
entries.statement: Fix q. There is a deterministic algorithm using polynomially many field operations in the tensor size that, from an arbitrary tensor A over F_q, outputs three bounded monomial equations defining its stabilizer determinant image, without enumerating its automorphism group.

entries.title: Contractions transport their kernels and images
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: Let finite-dimensional spaces over a field K carry a tensor t in U⊗V⊗W, and let g=(a,b,c) be invertible. The contraction C_t:U*→V⊗W satisfies C_{gt}=(b⊗c)C_t a*, where a*(λ)=λ∘a. Consequently its image, kernel, and every exterior-power rank certificate are transported by these explicit maps.

entries.title: Semi-invariants constrain, and sometimes identify, transporter characters
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: Let G act on X and let f:X→K satisfy f(gx)=χ(g)f(x), with χ:G→K× a character. If f(x)≠0, then χ(G_x)=1 and every transporter g:x→y satisfies χ(g)=f(y)/f(x). For several such functions with combined character φ, if y∈Gx and G_x=ker φ, their nonzero ratios determine the transporter coset exactly.

entries.title: Weight-zero monomials describe torus invariants
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: Let the algebraic torus (K×)^r act diagonally on K[x_1,…,x_n], with integer weights w_j∈Z^r, and assume K is infinite. Its invariant polynomials are precisely the K-linear combinations of monomials x^α with Σα_jw_j=0.

entries.title: Diagonal covariants are explicit weight-matching polynomials
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: In the setting of A033, suppose a finite-dimensional target E has a basis e_i with weights v_i. A polynomial map F:K^n→E is equivariant exactly when every monomial occurring in its ith coordinate has weight v_i, using the coordinate-action convention of A033 consistently.

entries.title: Averaging makes finite-group invariants exact
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: Let a finite group G act K-linearly, with |G| invertible in K. The averaging operator R(v)=|G|⁻¹Σ_g gv is a projection onto V^G. For every surjective equivariant map V→W, the induced map V^G→W^G is surjective.

entries.title: Finite-group polynomial invariants are finitely generated
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: For any finite group G acting linearly on A=K[x_1,…,x_n], the algebra A^G is finitely generated over K, in every characteristic.

entries.title: Finite orbits are separated by invariant polynomials
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: For a finite linear group G over any field K, two distinct G-orbits of K-rational vectors are separated by an invariant polynomial.

entries.title: Every stabilizer-fixed vector is a covariant value
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: Let G be finite with |G| invertible in K, acting linearly on V and E. For x∈V, evaluation of polynomial equivariant maps V→E onto E^{G_x} is surjective.

entries.title: Polynomial covariants form a finite module
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: For a finite group G and a finite-dimensional representation E, the covariant module (A⊗E)^G is finite over A^G, without a characteristic restriction.

entries.title: Nonmodular invariants commute with quotient by a stable ideal
entries.section: IV. Polynomial invariants and usable covariants
entries.statement: If |G| is invertible and I is a G-stable ideal of a G-algebra A, then the natural homomorphism A^G/(I∩A^G)→(A/I)^G is an isomorphism.

entries.title: Endomorphisms of a diagram form a computable algebra
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: A representation M of a finite quiver assigns finite-dimensional spaces M_v and arrow maps A_e. Its endomorphisms are tuples X_v satisfying X_{head(e)}A_e=A_eX_{tail(e)}. They form a unital finite-dimensional K-algebra, obtained as the kernel of an explicit linear system.

entries.title: Diagram automorphisms are exactly the units of the endomorphism algebra
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: An endomorphism X of M is a unit precisely when every X_v is invertible; its inverse is the tuple X_v⁻¹.

entries.title: Idempotents are precisely direct-sum projectors
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: An idempotent e in End(M) gives M=im e⊕ker e as quiver representations. Conversely every direct-sum decomposition gives such an idempotent; nontrivial decompositions correspond to e≠0,1.

entries.title: Fitting decomposition for a diagram endomorphism
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: For X∈End(M), sufficiently large N gives M=ker X^N⊕im X^N. Both are subrepresentations and X is nilpotent on the first and invertible on the second. If M is indecomposable, every endomorphism is either invertible or nilpotent.

entries.title: The endomorphism ring of an indecomposable finite diagram is local
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: For a nonzero indecomposable M, the nonunits of End(M) form a two-sided ideal; the quotient by it is a division ring.

entries.title: Krull–Schmidt uniqueness for finite-dimensional quiver representations
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: Every such representation is a finite direct sum of indecomposables, uniquely up to permutation and isomorphism of the summands.

entries.title: Intertwiner spaces commute with field extension
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: For finite diagrams M,N over K and an extension L/K, L⊗_K Hom(M,N) is naturally Hom(M_L,N_L).

entries.title: Isomorphism of finite diagrams descends over infinite fields
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: Let K be infinite. If M_L≅N_L over an extension L/K, then M≅N over K.

entries.title: A finite-field size bound also descends diagram isomorphisms
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: Over K=F_q, the conclusion of A048 holds whenever q>D=Σ_v dim M_v.

entries.title: Semisimple diagrams have canonical central blocks
entries.section: V. Intertwiner algebras and constructive decomposition
entries.statement: If M=⊕_{i=1}^r S_i^{m_i}, where the S_i are pairwise nonisomorphic simple finite-dimensional representations, then End(M)≅∏_i M_{m_i}(D_i), D_i=End(S_i) a division ring. Its primitive central idempotents project onto the isotypic summands.

entries.title: Two flags admit a common adapted basis
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: Given increasing flags U_0=0⊂⋯⊂U_a=V and W_0=0⊂⋯⊂W_b=V, there are subspaces E_{ij} with U_i∩W_j=⊕_{k≤i,l≤j}E_{kl}.

entries.title: Intersection dimensions classify pairs of flags
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: Two pairs of flags with identical index sets are related by an invertible linear map precisely when all corresponding dimensions dim(U_i∩W_j) agree. The numbers e_{ij}=dim F_{ij}−dim F_{i−1,j}−dim F_{i,j−1}+dim F_{i−1,j−1} are nonnegative and give a complete invariant.

entries.title: The flag stabilizer is an extension by a split unipotent group
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: For a flag with successive dimensions d_i, its stabilizer P maps onto ∏_i GL_{d_i}(K) by its action on successive quotients. The kernel consists of identity-diagonal block triangular matrices, and det g is the product of the graded determinants.

entries.title: Prescribed graded isomorphisms lift, with no extra determinant obstruction
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: Given two flags with equal successive dimensions and chosen isomorphisms on their corresponding graded spaces, there is a flag isomorphism inducing exactly them. Its determinant relative to chosen adapted volume bases is the product of their determinants; every other lift differs by the kernel of A053.

entries.title: Common flag stabilizers have a poset-triangular description
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: In the common decomposition of A051, a linear endomorphism preserves both flags exactly when its E_{ij}→E_{kl} blocks vanish unless k≤i and l≤j. The invertible such maps surject onto ∏_{ij}GL(E_{ij}); their kernel is identity plus a nilpotent block ideal, and their determinant is the product of diagonal determinants.

entries.title: All feasible nested subspace choices form an interval lattice
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: Let lower and upper subspaces L_t,U_t⊂V be specified for 1≤t≤r. Increasing choices L_t⊂X_t⊂U_t exist exactly when Σ_{s≤t}L_s⊂∩_{u≥t}U_u for every t. When they exist, their least and greatest choices are respectively those cumulative sums and future intersections; pointwise sums and intersections preserve feasibility.

entries.title: Nested containment constraints admit an invertible witness exactly by dimensions
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: For two increasing chains U_i,V_i in spaces of the same dimension N, there is an invertible f with f(U_i)⊂V_i for all i if and only if dim U_i≤dim V_i for all i.

entries.title: Paired inverse-transpose maps are exactly the two-Lagrangian symplectic stabilizer
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: On V⊕V* with ω((v,λ),(w,μ))=μ(v)−λ(w), the map diag(A,A⁻ᵀ) is symplectic and has determinant1. Conversely every symplectic map preserving V and V* individually has this form.

entries.title: Lagrangian graphs have explicit symplectic chart transitions
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: In V⊕V* with the pairing of A058, half-dimensional subspaces transverse to V* are graphs of unique S:V→V*. Such a graph is Lagrangian exactly when S(v)(w)=S(w)(v). For a symplectic block map g=[[a,b],[c,d]], its image of graph S is transverse to V* exactly when a+bS is invertible. On precisely that chart its new graph map is T=(c+dS)(a+bS)⁻¹, which is symmetric if and only if S is symmetric. These statements hold in every characteristic.

entries.title: Uniform unmarked tensor recovery of paired flags
entries.section: VI. Flags, adapted coordinates, and paired geometry
entries.statement: For each field K, seek a uniform polynomial-size construction from two finite flags in V to a single ordinary order-three tensor T, with no externally marked summands, such that a distinguished intrinsic quotient of T recovers V and both flags, and the induced map Aut(T)→GL(V) has image exactly the common flag stabilizer. The construction must also lift every member of that stabilizer. This precise package is **not proved here**; no assertion of global novelty or global openness is made.

entries.title: Coprime powers have an explicit inverse on bounded torsion
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: In any group, if x^n=1 and gcd(m,n)=1 with n>0, then x has a unique mth root in the cyclic subgroup it generates. If um+vn=1, that root is x^u. More generally the mth-power map is an automorphism on any abelian group of exponent dividing n.

entries.title: Nonzero Kummer fibres are separable root torsors
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: If n>0 is invertible in a field K and a∈K×, then T^n−a is separable. Over a field containing a root b and all nth roots of unity, its roots are exactly bμ_n, freely and transitively acted on by μ_n. The algebra K[T]/(T^n−a) is a product of finite separable field extensions.

entries.title: The norm is a multiplicative determinant with exact scalar powers
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: For a finite extension L/K of degree d, N_{L/K}(b)=det_K(m_b), m_b(x)=bx, is multiplicative; it is nonzero exactly when b≠0, and N_{L/K}(a)=a^d for a∈K.

entries.title: Restriction-of-scalars determinants are norms of determinants
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: For A∈M_n(L), det_K(A acting on L^n)=N_{L/K}(det_L A). Consequently norms are transitive in finite towers.

entries.title: Coprime extension degree forces root descent
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: Let [L:K]=d, a∈K×, b∈L× and b^n=a, with n>0 and gcd(n,d)=1. If ud+vn=1 then c=N_{L/K}(b)^u a^v∈K× satisfies c^n=a.

entries.title: Coupled scalar determinant corrections descend together
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: Let n_i>0 for i=1,2,3 and [L:K]=d coprime to N=lcm(n_1,n_2,n_3). Suppose a_i∈K× and b_i∈L× satisfy b_i^{n_i}=a_i and b_1b_2b_3=1. There are c_i∈K× with c_i^{n_i}=a_i and c_1c_2c_3=1.

entries.title: Split-torus monomial image membership descends in coprime degree
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: Let M be an integer matrix with nonzero Smith entries d_1,…,d_r>0. For [L:K]=e coprime to every d_i, a target y∈(K×)^s belongs to M((L×)^n) exactly when it belongs to M((K×)^n).

entries.title: Finite-field norms are surjective with equal fibres
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: For F_{q^d}/F_q, the norm is b↦b^{(q^d−1)/(q−1)}. It maps the multiplicative group onto F_q×, with every nonzero fibre of size (q^d−1)/(q−1).

entries.title: Marked coefficient actions recover extension-linear transporters
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: For finite-dimensional L-spaces V,W, a K-linear map f:V→W is L-linear precisely when it commutes with multiplication by a set of K-algebra generators of L. With those actions marked, restriction of scalars neither loses nor introduces isomorphisms of L-linear tensor or algebra diagrams.

entries.title: Quadratic norm-one elements have a rational parameter chart
entries.section: VII. Norms, restriction of scalars, and determinant descent
entries.statement: Let char K≠2 and L=K(u), u²=d∈K× nonsquare. Every norm-one z∈L× other than−1 has a unique form z=(1+tu)/(1−tu), t∈K. Every such expression has norm1; −1 is the omitted point.

entries.title: Fixed character values place the lifting obstruction in the kernel
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: Let φ:H→D be a group homomorphism commuting with automorphisms F of both groups. If φ(h) is F-fixed then c=h⁻¹F(h) belongs to the F-stable subgroup N=ker φ.

entries.title: Fixed lifts are exactly kernel Lang corrections
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: In A071 an F-fixed lift of φ(h) exists exactly when c=nF(n)⁻¹ for some n∈N. These lifts are precisely h n for such n. Replacing the initial lift by h b, b∈N, changes the obstruction to b⁻¹cF(b).

entries.title: Nonempty fixed fibres are torsors with exact counts
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: An F-fixed lift h_0 of d gives a bijection N^F→{h:Fh=h, φ(h)=d}, n↦h_0n. For finite groups every nonempty fixed fibre therefore has |N^F| elements.

entries.title: Component correction plus an internal Lang solution suffices
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: Let J≤N be F-stable and suppose every j∈J has form aF(a)⁻¹ with a∈J. If b∈N satisfies b⁻¹cF(b)∈J, then φ(h) has an F-fixed lift.

entries.title: The twisted obstruction norm telescopes
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: For c=h⁻¹F(h) and r>0, cF(c)⋯F^{r−1}(c)=h⁻¹F^r(h). An F^r-fixed initial lift therefore has twisted norm1.

entries.title: Weighted multiplicative averaging gives explicit corrections
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: Let N be abelian, F^r=1, and c∈N. Put B=∏_{i=0}^{r−1}F^i(c)^{r−1−i} and P=∏_{i=0}^{r−1}F^i(c). Then B/F(B)=c^r/P. If P=1 and c has order m coprime to r, choose k with rk≡1 mod m; n=B^k solves c=n/F(n).

entries.title: Coprime cyclic norm-one is exactly the correction criterion
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: For finite abelian N, F^r=1 and gcd(r,|N|)=1, an element c has twisted norm1 precisely when c=n/F(n) for some n∈N.

entries.title: Primary components solve abelian corrections independently
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: For finite abelian N, every primary subgroup N_ℓ is F-stable and N=∏_ℓN_ℓ. A correction c=n/F(n) exists precisely when it exists in each primary component; component solutions multiply to a global solution.

entries.title: Invariant characters detect every finite abelian correction obstruction
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: For finite abelian N, c lies in I={n/F(n)} exactly when χ(c)=1 for every complex character χ with χ∘F=χ.

entries.title: Cyclic kernels give explicit congruence tests and all solutions
entries.section: VIII. Frobenius and cyclic correction equations
entries.statement: Let N=⟨z⟩ have order m>0 and F(z)=z^q, gcd(q,m)=1. For c=z^a, the correction equation is solvable exactly when g=gcd(m,1−q) divides a, and then has exactly g solutions.

entries.title: Distinct field homomorphisms are linearly independent
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: Distinct field homomorphisms σ_1,…,σ_r:L→E are linearly independent as functions over E.

entries.title: Cyclic Hilbert90 has an explicit construction
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: For a cyclic Galois extension L/K with generator σ of order r, a∈L× has norm1 exactly when a=b/σ(b) for some b∈L×.

entries.title: Every finite Galois extension contains an element of trace1
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: For finite Galois L/K with group Γ, including characteristic dividing [L:K], some t∈L satisfies Σ_σσ(t)=1.

entries.title: Fixed vectors span every semilinear Galois representation
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: If a finite-dimensional L-space V has a semilinear action of the finite Galois group Γ of L/K, then V^Γ spans V over L.

entries.title: Semilinear descent reconstructs a basis over the fixed field
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: The map L⊗_K V^Γ→V, a⊗v↦av, is an isomorphism. In particular dim_K V^Γ=dim_L V.

entries.title: Matrix Hilbert90 reconstructs a simultaneous change of basis
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: For A_σ∈GL_n(L) satisfying A_{στ}=A_σσ(A_τ), some B∈GL_n(L) satisfies A_σ=Bσ(B)⁻¹ for all σ. Conversely every such B gives a cocycle.

entries.title: Morphisms, exact sequences, tensors and duals descend
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: For semilinear Γ-spaces U,V, equivariant L-linear maps correspond bijectively to K-linear maps U^Γ→V^Γ. Fixed vectors preserve short exact sequences and commute with tensor products and duals.

entries.title: Galois-stable subspaces are defined over the base field
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: A coordinatewise Γ-stable subspace W⊂L^n is the L-span of W∩K^n; L⊗_K(W∩K^n)→W is an isomorphism.

entries.title: Compatible algebra and tensor operations descend with their identities
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: A finite-dimensional L-algebra with semilinear Γ-action by algebra automorphisms is obtained by scalar extension from its fixed K-algebra. The same holds for finite families of multilinear operations and equivariant units. Structure-coefficient polynomial identities and nondegeneracy of bilinear forms descend.

entries.title: Galois-stable polynomial ideals descend coefficientwise
entries.section: IX. Galois descent with reconstructed witnesses
entries.statement: A coefficientwise Γ-stable ideal I⊂L[x_1,…,x_n] is generated as an ideal by I∩K[x_1,…,x_n].

entries.title: Schur complements preserve rank, determinant and explicit solutions
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: For M=[[A,B],[C,D]] with A invertible set S=D−CA⁻¹B. Then rank M=dim A+rank S; when square, det M=det A·det S. Its kernel is {(-A⁻¹By,y):Sy=0}.

entries.title: Rank-one updates have exact determinant and inverse tests
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: For invertible A and columns u,v, det(A+uvᵀ)=det A·(1+vᵀA⁻¹u). If s=1+vᵀA⁻¹u≠0, the inverse is A⁻¹−A⁻¹uvᵀA⁻¹/s; if s=0 it is singular.

entries.title: Rank normal forms give explicit, field-stable certificates
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: For an m×n matrix M of rank r, invertible P,Q give PMQ=diag(I_r,0) in rectangular block form. The last n−r columns of Q form a kernel basis and the first r columns of MQ form an image basis. The same certificate holds after every field extension.

entries.title: A nonzero minor reconstructs a subspace in a rational chart
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: If an r-dimensional W⊂K^n projects isomorphically onto some r coordinates I, it has a unique basis matrix C whose I-rows are I_r. Each other entry is a signed ratio of r×r minors of any basis matrix, and these chart entries determine W.

entries.title: Matrix-space invertibility has a bounded evaluation certificate
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: If the span of n×n matrices M_i over K contains an invertible evaluation over an extension, then every finite S⊂K with |S|>n has some z∈S^s for which Σz_iM_i is invertible. More generally a nonzero polynomial of total degree d has at most d|S|^{s−1} zeros in S^s.

entries.title: Modular nullspace reconstruction has an exact height certificate
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: Let an integer matrix C have rank r>0 and entries bounded in absolute value by B≥1. Choose a nonzero r×r minor D. Its pivot-equation kernel basis has reduced rational numerators and denominators bounded by H=r!B^r. Every prime p∤D preserves the chosen pivot rank r. Rational entries of these bounds, with denominators coprime to M, are uniquely determined by residues modulo M when M>2H².

entries.title: A short finite extension contains a nonsingular evaluation
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: A matrix space over F_q with an invertible extension-field evaluation has one over F_{q^e} whenever q^e>n. For n≥1 one may take e=1+⌊log_q n⌋.

entries.title: Invariant hulls stabilize within the ambient dimension
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: For endomorphisms T_1,…,T_s on an N-dimensional space, iteration W_0=W, W_{j+1}=W_j+Σ_iT_iW_j reaches the least common invariant subspace containing W after at most N−dim W strict steps.

entries.title: First-order diagram deformations form an explicit linear quotient
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: For a quiver representation with polynomial relations, write arrow maps over K[ε]/(ε²) as A_e+εB_e. Their relation constraints form a linear space Z. Basis changes I+εX_v shift B_e by X_{head(e)}A_e−A_eX_{tail(e)}; these shifts form a subspace B⊂Z. First-order equivalence classes with identity reduction are exactly Z/B. The shift map's kernel is End(M).

entries.title: Fixed-dimensional unipotent transporter fibres have polynomial-height points
entries.section: X. Exact certificates and controlled reconstruction
entries.statement: Fix dimensions of three rational tensor factors. For tensors x,y over Q with reduced entry numerators and denominators bounded by H≥2, suppose a rational GL-transporter exists and the effective algebraic stabilizer G_x/Z is a split unipotent Q-group, where G=GL(U)×GL(V)×GL(W) and Z={(aI_U,bI_V,cI_W):abc=1} is the central kernel. Seek C depending only on the dimensions such that some rational transporter has all reduced entry numerators and denominators bounded by H^C. This is **not proved here** and is not asserted globally new or globally open.

entries.title: Affine lines form an explicit resolvable design [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: Let F be a finite field of order q. On F², the q vertical lines x=c and, for each a in F, the q lines y=ax+b form q+1 parallel classes. Every line has q points; every class partitions F²; two lines from distinct classes meet exactly once. Every pair of distinct points lies on exactly one of these lines.

entries.title: Projective completion of the affine plane [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: Adding one point for each of the q+1 directions in B001 and a line containing exactly those points gives a projective plane with q²+q+1 points and the same number of lines. Every line has q+1 points, every point lies on q+1 lines, and distinct points or distinct lines determine a unique incident line or intersection point.

entries.title: Exact singular spectrum of projective incidence [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: If N is the point-by-line 0–1 incidence matrix of B002 and v=q²+q+1, then NN*=qI+J. Its singular values are q+1 once and √q with multiplicity v−1. Consequently N is invertible over R.

entries.title: Higher-dimensional projective point and hyperplane counts [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: In an n-dimensional F_q-vector space with n≥2, the number of one-dimensional subspaces and of hyperplanes is v=(q^n−1)/(q−1). Every hyperplane contains k=(q^(n−1)−1)/(q−1) projective points; each pair of distinct projective points lies in λ=(q^(n−2)−1)/(q−1) hyperplanes.

entries.title: Counting Lagrangian subspaces [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: A nondegenerate alternating form on F_q^(2n) has exactly ∏_{i=1}^n(q^i+1) Lagrangian subspaces, including the value 1 when n=0.

entries.title: Symmetric matrices parametrize transverse Lagrangians [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: In F_q^n⊕F_q^n with form ω((x,y),(x',y'))=x·y'−y·x', the graph L_A={(x,Ax)} is Lagrangian precisely when A is symmetric. Moreover dim(L_A∩L_B)=dim ker(A−B).

entries.title: An explicit symplectic spread from field multiplication [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: Let p be prime, r≥1, E=F_(p^r), q=p^r, and use ω((x,y),(x',y'))=Tr_E/Fp(xy'−yx'). The q subspaces L_a={(x,ax):x∈E}, together with L_∞={(0,y)}, are r-dimensional F_p-Lagrangians partitioning E²\{0}.

entries.title: A verifiable hole-filling criterion for partial spreads [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: Suppose a family of pairwise disjoint n-dimensional isotropic subspaces of a 2n-dimensional symplectic F_q-space is given. Let H consist of zero and all nonzero vectors uncovered by the family. If H is closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication, has q^n elements, and is isotropic, then adjoining H extends the partial spread to a full spread.

entries.title: A clique certificate that constructs a symplectic spread [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: Let A be a set of q^n symmetric n-by-n matrices over F_q such that A−B is invertible whenever A≠B. Their graphs together with L_∞ form a symplectic spread.

entries.title: Every isotropic subspace has a constructive Lagrangian extension [proved]
entries.section: 1. Finite incidence geometry and symplectic constructions
entries.statement: If U is isotropic in a nondegenerate 2n-dimensional alternating space, then U is contained in a Lagrangian. One can construct it by at most n−dim U single-vector extensions.

entries.title: The incidence operator of a 2-design [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: Let a finite incidence structure have v points, b blocks of size k, each point in r blocks, and each distinct pair of points in λ blocks. Its incidence matrix N satisfies NN*=(r−λ)I+λJ, vr=bk, and r(k−1)=λ(v−1).

entries.title: A symmetric design supplies a regular simplex [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: Suppose B011 is symmetric, b=v and r=k, with 0<k<v. Center each row of N by subtracting (k/v)1. After normalization, the v resulting real vectors have pairwise inner product −1/(v−1) and span a (v−1)-dimensional space.

entries.title: Fisher's inequality with an explicit reconstruction map [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: Under B011, if r>λ≥0, then b≥v and the map N*:R^v→R^b is injective. Data y=N*x reconstruct x by x=((r−λ)I+λJ)^−1Ny.

entries.title: Resolutions produce orthogonal contrast spaces [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: Let v=sk points be partitioned into s blocks of size k in each of t parallel classes. Assume blocks from different classes meet in k/s points. The centered indicators u_B=1_B−1/s·1 span mutually orthogonal (s−1)-dimensional spaces D_a. Within one class ∑_B u_Bu_B*=kΠ_(D_a). If t(s−1)=v−1, all centered indicators form a k-tight frame for 1⊥.

entries.title: Nets and flat matrices construct MUBs [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: Suppose s² points admit t parallel classes, each partitioning them into s blocks of size s, with any blocks from different classes intersecting once. If H is an s-by-s unitary matrix all of whose entries have modulus 1/√s, then these data construct t MUBs in C^(s²).

entries.title: Orthogonal Latin squares give the net input explicitly [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: A family of m pairwise orthogonal Latin squares of order s gives m+2 classes satisfying B015, hence m+2 MUBs in C^(s²). Over F_q, the q−1 squares L_a(x,y)=ax+y for a≠0 give q+1 such bases.

entries.title: Laplacian energy reconstructs connected components [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: For a finite undirected simple graph with adjacency A and degree matrix D, L=D−A is positive semidefinite, and ker L consists exactly of functions constant on each connected component. Hence its nullity equals the number of components.

entries.title: A spectral gap is a quantitative averaging criterion [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: If a connected graph has smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue γ>0, then for every vector x, ||x−mean(x)1||²≤γ^−1∑_{edges}|x_i−x_j|². Replacing x by its mean is therefore a certified approximate solution of all equality constraints along edges.

entries.title: Expander mixing from a directly checkable spectrum [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: In a k-regular graph on n≥1 vertices, assume ||A|_(1⊥)||≤λ. For vertex sets S,T, let e(S,T)=1_SᵀA1_T, counting oriented incidences. Then |e(S,T)−k|S||T|/n|≤λ√(|S|(1−|S|/n)|T|(1−|T|/n)).

entries.title: A dense compatibility graph contains a constructive clique [proved]
entries.section: 2. Design matrices and spectral construction tools
entries.statement: Let r≥2 and let a simple graph on N vertices have minimum degree δ>N(1−1/(r−1)). Then it contains a clique of size r, obtainable by successive common-neighbor choices.

entries.title: Synthesis and Gram operators have the same positive spectrum [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: For a d-by-N complex matrix F with columns f_i, put S=FF* and G=F*F. Their positive eigenvalues, with multiplicity, agree. In particular span{f_i}=C^d exactly when S is positive definite.

entries.title: Canonical duals reconstruct and control measurement noise [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: If S=∑f_if_i* satisfies S≥aI with a>0, set g_i=S^−1f_i. Then x=∑g_i⟨f_i,x⟩. If the measured coefficients have error e∈C^N, the reconstruction error has norm at most ||e||/√a.

entries.title: Frame potential equality constructs tightness [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: If N≥1 and f_1,…,f_N are unit vectors in C^d, their frame potential FP=∑_{i,j}|⟨f_i,f_j⟩|² satisfies FP≥N²/d. Equality holds exactly when ∑f_if_i*=(N/d)I.

entries.title: Polar whitening is a quantitative Parseval repair [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: If S=∑f_if_i*>0, the vectors g_i=S^−1/2f_i satisfy ∑g_ig_i*=I. If ||S−I||≤ε<1, then ||S^−1/2−I||≤(1−ε)^−1/2−1.

entries.title: Naimark complementation constructs a second tight frame [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: If F is d-by-N, FF*=I and every column has squared norm d/N, with 0<d<N, there is an (N−d)-by-N matrix H with HH*=I and H*H=I−F*F. After normalizing its columns, it is a unit-norm tight frame, and its off-diagonal Gram entries are −d/(N−d) times those of the unit-normalized F-columns.

entries.title: Direct sums and tensors preserve explicit tight-frame identities [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: If frames in H_1,H_2 have tight bounds c_1,c_2, their tensor-product vectors form a c_1c_2-tight frame on H_1⊗H_2. Their disjoint direct-sum embeddings form a tight frame on H_1⊕H_2 exactly when c_1=c_2.

entries.title: Irreducible unitary orbits are tight [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: Let a finite group act irreducibly and unitarily on C^d. For x≠0, the indexed orbit (U_gx)_(g∈G) is a tight frame of bound |G|||x||²/d.

entries.title: Balanced seeds work for multiplicity-free representations [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: Suppose a finite group's unitary representation is the orthogonal sum of pairwise inequivalent irreducibles H_j of dimensions d_j, and d=∑d_j. A unit seed x has tight orbit precisely when ||Π_jx||²=d_j/d for every j.

entries.title: A deterministic erasure budget preserves reconstruction [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement: If S=∑f_if_i*≥aI and ||f_i||²≤μ, removing any r vectors leaves a frame whenever a−rμ>0. Its canonical-dual noise amplification is at most (a−rμ)^−1/2.

entries.title: Weighted minimum-noise reconstruction is uniquely optimal [proved]
entries.section: 3. Finite frames as explicit linear reconstruction devices
entries.statement:
Let F be a d×N complex matrix of row rank d, where d≥1, and let Σ be a positive definite N×N Hermitian matrix. Put S=FΣ⁻¹F* and L₀=S⁻¹FΣ⁻¹. Then L₀F*=I. Every other exact linear reconstruction L, meaning LF*=I, has the covariance identity

LΣL*=S⁻¹+(L−L₀)Σ(L−L₀)*.

Consequently L₀ minimizes the reconstruction-noise covariance in positive-semidefinite order and uniquely minimizes its trace. This applies to measurements y=F*x+ε with mean-zero noise of covariance Σ.

entries.title: Spectral defects give optimal arbitrary-vector completions [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: Given S=∑f_if_i* and c>0 with c≥λ_max(S), put D=cI−S. Adding vectors whose rank-one operators sum to D completes the family to a c-tight frame. The smallest possible number of nonzero added vectors is rank D.

entries.title: Every Hermitian matrix has a constant-diagonal basis [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: A Hermitian operator A on C^n, n≥1, admits an orthonormal basis e_j with ⟨e_j,Ae_j⟩=tr(A)/n for every j.

entries.title: Exact equal-norm defect completion [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: Let D≥0 on C^d and let N≥1 and t>0. There exist N vectors z_j with ||z_j||²=t and ∑z_jz_j*=D exactly when tr D=Nt and rank D≤N.

entries.title: Unit-norm tight frames exist for every N≥d [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: For integers N≥d≥1, take the first d rows of the N-by-N Fourier unitary and multiply them by √(N/d). The resulting N columns are unit vectors and form an (N/d)-tight frame in C^d.

entries.title: A unit-norm frame can be completed without changing old vectors [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: Given m unit vectors in C^d with frame operator S and a proposed N≥1 extra vectors, put c=(m+N)/d. If c≥λ_max(S) and rank(cI−S)≤N, there is a c-tight unit-norm completion by exactly N additional vectors.

entries.title: A two-column block spends fractional spectral mass exactly [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: For 0≤x≤2 the real unit vectors a=(√(x/2),√(1−x/2)) and b=(√(x/2),−√(1−x/2)) satisfy aaᵀ+bbᵀ=diag(x,2−x).

entries.title: Spectral tetris for spectra bounded below by two [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: If λ_1,…,λ_d≥2 and N=∑λ_i is an integer, there is a real unit-norm frame with frame operator diag(λ_1,…,λ_d), each column supported on at most two coordinates.

entries.title: Projection defects construct equal-rank fusion completions [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: Suppose orthogonal projections P_i and a scalar c satisfy D=cI−∑P_i≥0 and D²=D. If rank D=mk for integers m≥0,k≥1, then m rank-k orthogonal projections Q_j can be added so that ∑P_i+∑Q_j=cI.

entries.title: Two nontrivial projections can be tight only by complementing [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: If P is an orthogonal projection with both nonzero range and nonzero kernel, and Q is another orthogonal projection satisfying P+Q=cI, then c=1 and Q=I−P. Conversely this choice always works.

entries.title: Finite unitary orbits construct tight fusion frames [proved]
entries.section: 4. Constructive tight-frame and fusion-frame completion
entries.statement: Let an irreducible finite unitary group act on C^d and let P have rank k with 1≤k≤d. The indexed projections U_gPU_g* sum to (|G|k/d)I.

entries.title: The tensor-power Welch inequality with equality data [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: For N≥1 unit vectors x_1,…,x_N in C^d and integer t≥1, set D_t=binom(d+t−1,t). Then ∑_{i,j}|⟨x_i,x_j⟩|^(2t)≥N²/D_t. Equality means ∑|x_i^⊗t⟩⟨x_i^⊗t|=(N/D_t)I on Sym^t(C^d).

entries.title: A finite second-moment identity defines a projective 2-design [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: A family of unit vectors with positive weights w_i summing to one is a complex projective 2-design exactly when ∑w_i P_i⊗P_i=2Π_sym/[d(d+1)], where Π_sym=(I+Swap)/2. In particular its weighted fourth-overlap potential is at least 2/[d(d+1)], with equality exactly for this identity.

entries.title: Second-moment designs reconstruct every matrix [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement:
For a weighted design in B042 and any complex d-by-d matrix A,
∑w_i tr(AP_i)P_i=(A+tr(A)I)/[d(d+1)]. Consequently its rank-one projectors span the full complex matrix space.

entries.title: Design measurements have a closed reconstruction formula [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: For B042, the operators E_i=dw_iP_i form a positive operator-valued measurement. If tr ρ=1 and p_i=tr(ρE_i), then ρ=(d+1)∑p_iP_i−I.

entries.title: Complete MUBs give a projective 2-design [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: In dimension d≥2, the union of d+1 pairwise unbiased orthonormal bases, with uniform weight on its N=d(d+1) vectors, is a projective 2-design.

entries.title: A SIC equality certificate gives a 2-design [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: If d² unit vectors in C^d have |⟨x_i,x_j⟩|²=1/(d+1) whenever i≠j, their uniform measure is a projective 2-design.

entries.title: SIC projectors form a minimal informationally complete simplex [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement:
Under B046 with d≥2, put Y_i=P_i−I/d. Their Gram matrix has diagonal (d−1)/d and off-diagonal −1/[d(d+1)]. They span the traceless Hermitian space, satisfy ∑Y_i=0, and for every Hermitian A,
A=(d+1)/d∑tr(AP_i)P_i−tr(A)I.

entries.title: Approximate moment operators still give stable tomography [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: Let unit vectors and weights define T(A)=∑w_i tr(AP_i)P_i on the real Hilbert space of Hermitian matrices. If ||T−T_0||≤ε<1/[d(d+1)], where T_0(A)=(A+tr(A)I)/[d(d+1)], then T is invertible and ||T^−1||≤(1/[d(d+1)]−ε)^−1.

entries.title: Design tomography tolerates a certified erasure set [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: For an unweighted projective 2-design of N unit vectors, the centered projectors Y_i=P_i−I/d form a tight frame of bound N/[d(d+1)] on traceless Hermitian matrices. Removing r of them preserves this spanning property if N/[d(d+1)]>r(d−1)/d.

entries.title: Product designs give explicit local tomography in composite dimensions [proved]
entries.section: 5. Tensor moments, projective designs, and informational completeness
entries.statement: If designs in C^a and C^b have tomography maps T_a,T_b from B043, their product measurement has map T_a⊗T_b on matrices on C^a⊗C^b. It is invertible, so it reconstructs arbitrary entangled states as well as product states.

entries.title: Unbiased bases are orthogonal diagonal contrast spaces [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: For an orthonormal basis B=(b_i), set Q_i=P_(b_i)−I/d and let D_B be their real span. Then dim D_B=d−1 and tr(Q_iQ_j)=δ_ij−1/d. Two bases B,C are unbiased exactly when D_B and D_C are Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal.

entries.title: The complex MUB bound follows with its equality decomposition [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: For d≥2, k pairwise unbiased bases have k≤d+1. If k=d+1, their spaces D_B are an orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of all traceless Hermitian matrices.

entries.title: Real unbiasedness has a different equality space [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: For d≥2, k pairwise unbiased real orthonormal bases satisfy k≤d/2+1. Equality gives an orthogonal decomposition of traceless real symmetric matrices by their diagonal contrast spaces.

entries.title: Collision probabilities obey an exact Bessel budget [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: If B_a are k MUBs and ρ is Hermitian of trace one, put p_ai=tr(ρP_ai). Then ∑_(a,i)(p_ai−1/d)²≤tr(ρ²)−1/d. Equality holds when ρ−I/d lies in ⊕_a D_(B_a).

entries.title: Complete MUBs reconstruct trace-one matrices [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: If d+1 MUBs are supplied and p_ai=tr(ρP_ai) for tr ρ=1, then ρ=∑_(a,i)p_aiP_ai−I.

entries.title: The residual operator is an explicit orthogonal projection [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement:
For k MUBs define, on Hermitian A,
R(A)=A−tr(A)I/d−∑_a[∑_i tr(AP_ai)P_ai−tr(A)I/d].
Then R projects orthogonally onto the traceless space perpendicular to every D_(B_a), of dimension d²−1−k(d−1).

entries.title: A rank-one residual witness gives an actual unbiased vector [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: A unit vector x is unbiased to every supplied basis B_a exactly when P_x−I/d belongs to ran R from B056. Equivalently, a positive semidefinite trace-one matrix P with tr(P²)=1 and P−I/d∈ran R constructs such a vector by taking its nonzero eigenvector.

entries.title: Commuting residual matrices suffice to construct a missing basis [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: If ran R contains d−1 real-linearly independent, pairwise commuting Hermitian matrices K_1,…,K_(d−1), then the supplied MUB family extends by one orthonormal basis.

entries.title: A simple-spectrum matrix yields a smaller extension certificate [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: Suppose a Hermitian H has d distinct eigenvalues and H^m−tr(H^m)I/d∈ran R for every m=1,…,d−1. Then its eigenbasis extends the supplied MUB family.

entries.title: A Hermitian channel supplies a constructive commuting certificate [proved]
entries.section: 6. MUB operator geometry and sufficient missing-basis certificates
entries.statement: Let Hermitian K_1,…,K_d be real-linearly independent, with ∑K_i²=I and Φ(K_j)=K_j for Φ(X)=∑K_iXK_i. If every old basis vector v satisfies ⟨v,K_iv⟩=tr(K_i)/d, then a common eigenbasis of the K_i is unbiased to every old basis.

entries.title: Finite Fourier matrices are unitary [proved]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: For G=∏_(j=1)^r Z/n_jZ with n_j≥1, the functions χ_a(x)=exp(2πi∑a_jx_j/n_j), normalized by |G|^−1/2, form an orthonormal basis of C^G. In particular a flat unitary exists in every positive integer dimension.

entries.title: The odd-prime quadratic Gauss magnitude [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: If p is odd prime, ζ=exp(2πi/p), a≠0 in F_p, and b∈F_p, then |∑_x ζ^(ax²+bx)|²=p.

entries.title: Chirps construct p+1 MUBs for every odd prime [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: In C^(F_p), let c_b^a(x)=p^−1/2ζ^(ax²+bx), for a,b∈F_p. For each a, the p vectors c_b^a form a basis. These p bases and the coordinate basis are p+1 MUBs.

entries.title: Trace characters extend the Gauss magnitude to odd prime powers [proved]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: Let E=F_(p^r) with p odd, q=|E|, and ψ(x)=exp(2πiTr(x)/p). For a≠0, |∑_(x∈E)ψ(ax²+bx)|²=q.

entries.title: Complete MUBs in every odd prime-power dimension [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: With E and ψ as in B064, the q vectors q^−1/2ψ(ax²+bx), indexed by b∈E, form a basis for each a∈E. Together with the coordinate basis these give q+1 MUBs in C^q.

entries.title: The qubit three-basis seed [proved]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: In C² the coordinate basis, {(1,1)/√2,(1,−1)/√2}, and {(1,i)/√2,(1,−i)/√2} are pairwise unbiased.

entries.title: Tensor products preserve the supplied number of MUBs [proved]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: If H_1 and H_2 have t_1 and t_2 MUBs, then H_1⊗H_2 has at least min(t_1,t_2) MUBs. In particular B063 and B066 construct three MUBs in C^6.

entries.title: Weyl matrices give an orthogonal unitary operator basis [proved]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: For E=F_(p^r), let X_a e_x=e_(x+a), Z_b e_x=ψ(bx)e_x, and W_(a,b)=X_aZ_b on C^E. The q² W_(a,b) are unitary and satisfy tr(W_u*W_v)=qδ_uv. Their commutator scalar is ψ(bc−da) for u=(a,b), v=(c,d).

entries.title: Disjoint isotropic Weyl classes construct unbiased bases [proved]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: Let L,M be r-dimensional F_p-isotropic subspaces of E² for the trace symplectic form, with L∩M={0}. Common eigenbases of {W_l:l∈L} and {W_m:m∈M} are unbiased.

entries.title: A symplectic spread constructs a complete MUB family [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 7. Explicit character, Gauss-sum, and Weyl constructions
entries.statement: Any spread of E² by r-dimensional F_p-isotropic subspaces produces q+1 MUBs in C^q. In particular B007 constructs complete MUB families in every prime-power dimension, including powers of two.

entries.title: A candidate graph can certify a missing unbiased basis [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Let X be a finite indexed set of unit vectors already unbiased to every old basis in C^d, d≥2. Connect two distinct indices when their vectors are orthogonal. A clique of size d constructs a new unbiased basis; the degree hypothesis of B020 with r=d is a sufficient certificate that such a clique exists.

entries.title: Positive rank-one moment certificates construct a basis [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Suppose d Hermitian matrices P_j are positive semidefinite, have tr P_j=tr(P_j²)=1, satisfy ∑P_j=I, and have tr(P_jP_ai)=1/d for every old basis projector. Then their nonzero eigenvectors form a new unbiased orthonormal basis.

entries.title: Partitioned orthogonal unitaries construct MUBs [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Suppose k classes each contain d−1 traceless, pairwise commuting unitary matrices, and together with I all the listed matrices are pairwise orthogonal for tr(U*V). Then their common eigenbases give k MUBs.

entries.title: Gauge normalization preserves all MUB constraints [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: A common unitary, permutations of bases and basis vectors, and independent unit-modulus phases on vectors preserve a MUB family. Any family with a chosen first basis can be normalized so that it is the coordinate basis; every other basis can then have its first row equal to the positive constant 1/√d.

entries.title: Multipartite exclusion budgets suffice for a basis transversal [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Let C_1,…,C_d be finite nonempty sets of unit vectors, all unbiased to the old family. Suppose for i<j every vector in C_i is nonorthogonal to at most a_ij vectors of C_j, and |C_j|>∑_(i<j)a_ij for every j≥2. Then one can choose x_j∈C_j forming a new unbiased basis.

entries.title: Deleting a flat-unitary row constructs a regular simplex [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Let H be an N-by-N unitary with entries of modulus 1/√N, N≥2. Delete one row and multiply the remaining matrix by √(N/(N−1)). Its columns are unit vectors forming a tight frame in C^(N−1), with all off-diagonal inner-product magnitudes 1/(N−1).

entries.title: A quadratic Seidel equation is a sufficient ETF certificate [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Let N>1 and S be Hermitian with zero diagonal, |S_ij|=1 for i≠j, and S²=(N−1)I+μS for a real μ. If ρ_-<0<ρ_+ are the two roots of t²−μt−(N−1), then G=I−S/ρ_- is the Gram matrix of a unit-norm equiangular tight frame.

entries.title: Symmetric conference matrices construct half-dimensional ETFs [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: If N≥2 and C is a real symmetric N-by-N matrix with zero diagonal, ±1 off-diagonal entries, and C²=(N−1)I, then N is even and I+C/√(N−1) constructs N equiangular unit vectors in R^(N/2), tight with bound two.

entries.title: Steiner designs and flat simplices construct sparse ETFs [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: A 2-(v,k,1) design with v>k≥2 has r=(v−1)/(k−1) blocks through each point and b=vr/k blocks. With a complex Hadamard matrix of order r+1, it constructs N=v(r+1) equiangular unit vectors in C^b, each supported on r coordinates, with common overlap magnitude 1/r.

entries.title: Weighted projective designs admit finite support reduction [proved]
entries.section: 8. Finite sufficient certificates for compatible bases and equiangular frames
entries.statement: Any finite weighted projective 2-design in C^d can be replaced by one supported on a subset of at most D² of its original vectors, where D=d(d+1)/2, preserving its exact moment identity and nonnegative weights summing to one.

entries.title: A flat codimension-one core determines all moduli [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Let U be an n-by-n complex matrix with n≥2 and U*U=cI for c>0. If |U_ij|²=c/n whenever i,j<n, then the same equality holds for every entry.

entries.title: Partial flat orthogonal columns have a flat completion [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Let n≥2 and A be n-by-(n−1), with A*A=nI and |A_ij|²=1 for i<n and all columns j. There is an n-by-n H with H*H=nI, all entries unimodular, and first n−1 columns exactly A.

entries.title: Simultaneous border completion preserves cross unbiasedness [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Let A_a be a finite family of matrices satisfying B082. If every entry of A_a*A_b has squared modulus n for a≠b, their individual completions H_a from B082, together with the coordinate basis after dividing each H_a by √n, form a MUB family.

entries.title: Flat border completion stays in the input conjugation field [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Under B082, let K⊂C be a field closed under complex conjugation and containing all entries of A. A flat completion can be chosen with entries in K and with the first entry of its last column equal to one. Any two completions differ only by a phase in that column.

entries.title: Polar correction repairs an almost-unitary square matrix [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: If ||U*U−I||≤ε<1, then V=U(U*U)^−1/2 is unitary and ||U−V||≤1−√(1−ε)=ε/(1+√(1−ε)).

entries.title: Overlap errors survive controlled vector repair [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: For unit x,y,x',y' with ||x−x'||≤α and ||y−y'||≤β, the squared overlap changes by at most 2(α+β). Therefore a finite table of approximate unbiasedness errors remains valid after repairs, with this explicitly added error budget per pair.

entries.title: An almost-fixed channel gives a commutator-energy bound [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement:
If Hermitian K_i satisfy ∑K_i²=I and Φ(X)=∑K_iXK_i, then for Hermitian X with ||Φ(X)−X||_HS≤η,
∑||[K_i,X]||_HS²≤2||X||_HSη.

entries.title: A spectral gap constructs a nearby commuting matrix [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Let A be Hermitian with distinct eigenvalues separated by γ>0, and B Hermitian. In an eigenbasis of A, let D_A(B) retain only the diagonal entries of B. Then D_A(B) commutes with A and ||B−D_A(B)||_HS≤||[A,B]||_HS/γ.

entries.title: Vandermonde conditioning quantifies the moment certificate [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Let H have d distinct real eigenvalues λ_j and eigenvectors e_j. For a unit v, put η_m=⟨v,H^mv⟩−tr(H^m)/d, 0≤m<d, and V_mj=λ_j^m. Then the vector r_j=|⟨e_j,v⟩|²−1/d satisfies r=V^−1η, so ||r||_2≤||V^−1||·||η||_2.

entries.title: A contraction certificate constructs an exact geometric configuration [proved]
entries.section: 9. Border completion and robust finite existence certificates
entries.statement: Let U_a(x) be specified complex matrix polynomials in x∈R^n. Let R_i(x) be all real and imaginary orthonormality residuals and all unbiasedness residuals d|(U_a*U_b)_jk|²−1. Supply a square polynomial system F:R^n→R^n, explicit polynomial identities R_i=∑h_ijF_j, an invertible real J, and a closed ball B(x_0,r), r>0. If sup_B||I−JF'(x)||≤θ<1 and ||JF(x_0)||≤(1−θ)r, then the ball contains x_* for which every U_a(x_*) is a member of a genuine MUB family.

entries.title: A fourth MUB in dimension six does not exist [conjecture; classical direction]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: Every family of pairwise unbiased orthonormal bases in C^6 has size at most three.

entries.title: Complete complex MUB families occur exactly in prime-power dimensions [conjecture; classical direction]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: For an integer d≥2, there exist d+1 MUBs in C^d if and only if d is a prime power.

entries.title: Weyl–Heisenberg SIC construction in every dimension [conjecture; classical direction]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: For every integer d≥2 there is a unit vector x∈C^d such that the d² rays of X^aZ^b x, with cyclic shift X, diagonal clock Z and a,b∈Z/dZ, have squared pairwise overlaps 1/(d+1).

entries.title: Paley's quadratic-character construction gives real Hadamard matrices [proved; classical reconstruction]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: If q is a prime power with q≡3 mod4, one can explicitly construct a real (q+1)-by-(q+1) matrix H with entries ±1 and HHᵀ=(q+1)I.

entries.title: Uniqueness of a complete MUB family in complex dimension seven [conjecture; atlas proposal]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: Every family of eight MUBs in C^7 is equivalent to B063's chirp family under a common unitary or antiunitary, basis permutations, vector permutations, and individual phases.

entries.title: A quantitative stability exponent for the qutrit complete family [conjecture; atlas proposal]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: For four unitary 3-by-3 matrices U_a, set Δ=∑_(a<b,i,j)(|(U_a*U_b)_ij|²−1/3)². Let dist be the square root of the sum of squared Frobenius distances to the orbit of the standard complete qutrit family under B074's equivalences. There exist constants C,ε>0 such that Δ≤ε implies dist≤CΔ^(1/4).

entries.title: Prime-phase codimension-one Hadamard completion [proved; atlas derivation, no novelty claim]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: If p is prime and A is a p-by-(p−1) matrix of pth roots of unity with A*A=pI, then it has a completion H with all entries pth roots of unity and H*H=pI, preserving every supplied column.

entries.title: Deficiency-one symplectic partial spreads always complete [proved; atlas derivation, no novelty claim]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: Let q be a prime power and n≥1. Any q^n pairwise trivially intersecting n-dimensional isotropic subspaces in a nondegenerate2n-dimensional alternating F_q-space extend uniquely to a full symplectic spread, by adjoining the uncovered nonzero vectors together with zero.

entries.title: Square-root normalized-Hilbert–Schmidt repair for three Hermitian matrices [conjecture; atlas proposal]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: There is a universal C such that for all d and Hermitian contractions A_1,A_2,A_3, writing δ=(∑_(i<j)||[A_i,A_j]||_(2,d)²)^(1/2), one can find commuting Hermitian contractions B_1,B_2,B_3 with (∑||A_i−B_i||_(2,d)²)^(1/2)≤Cδ^(1/2). Here ||X||_(2,d)=||X||_HS/√d, and all three matrices may move.

entries.title: Unweighted projective 2-designs at the MUB cardinality scale [conjecture; atlas proposal]
entries.section: 10. Research targets and three completed construction arguments
entries.statement: For every d≥2 there exist N≤d(d+1) pairwise distinct rank-one projectors in C^d whose uniform measure is a projective 2-design.

entries.title: Diminishing returns characterizes submodularity
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: Submodularity is equivalent to f(A∪{e})−f(A)≥f(B∪{e})−f(B) whenever A⊆B and e∉B.

entries.title: A greedy vector is a base-polytope certificate
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: Suppose f is normalized and submodular. For an ordering e₁,…,e_n, put P_i={e₁,…,e_i} and v(e_i)=f(P_i)−f(P_{i−1}). Then v(E)=f(E) and v(S)≤f(S) for every S⊆E.

entries.title: Exact support function of a submodular base polytope
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: Under C002, order any real weights w so w₁≥⋯≥w_n. Then max_{x∈B(f)}w·x=w_n f(E)+Σ_{i<n}(w_i−w_{i+1})f(P_i), attained by C002's vector. For E=∅ the maximum is zero.

entries.title: Tight sets uncross
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: If x(S)≤f(S) for all S and f is submodular, then sets A,B satisfying x(A)=f(A), x(B)=f(B) also have tight union and intersection.

entries.title: Submodular minimizers form a lattice
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: The minimizers of a submodular f over all subsets of E are closed under union and intersection. In particular they have a unique inclusion-minimal member and a unique inclusion-maximal member.

entries.title: Weighted cut submodularity with exact slack
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: For an undirected graph with nonnegative edge weights, c(S)=w(δS) is submodular, with c(A)+c(B)−c(A∪B)−c(A∩B)=2w(E(A\B,B\A)).

entries.title: Coverage functions are submodular
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: Given subsets S_e of a finite feature set U with nonnegative feature weights a_u, f(A)=Σ_{u∈∪_{e∈A}S_e}a_u is normalized, monotone and submodular.

entries.title: Greedy cardinality approximation
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: If f is normalized, nonnegative, monotone and submodular, and 1≤k≤|E|, repeatedly adding a largest-marginal unused element gives G_k with f(G_k)≥[1−(1−1/k)^k] max_{|S|≤k}f(S).

entries.title: Convexity of the Lovász extension
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: For normalized submodular f, define L_f(w)=Σ_i w_i[f(P_i)−f(P_{i−1})] using a nonincreasing ordering of the coordinates of w. This is well defined and convex on R^E.

entries.title: union-closed frequency one half
entries.section: 1. Submodularity, certificates and uncrossing
entries.statement: A finite union-closed family F containing a nonempty set has an element belonging to at least |F|/2 members.

entries.title: Rank is submodular
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: Matroid rank is normalized, integer valued, monotone, bounded by |A|, and submodular.

entries.title: Rank axioms reconstruct a matroid
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: Conversely, an integer-valued normalized monotone submodular r with 0≤r(A)≤|A| defines a matroid by declaring I independent exactly when r(I)=|I|; its rank function is r.

entries.title: Closure and the exchange law
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: Define cl(A)={e:r(A+e)=r(A)}. Then closure is monotone and idempotent. If e∈cl(A+f)\cl(A), then f∈cl(A+e).

entries.title: Fundamental circuits are unique
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: If I is independent and I+e is dependent, it has a unique minimal dependent subset C; it contains e. Moreover I−b+e is independent exactly when b∈C\{e}, for b∈I.

entries.title: Symmetric basis exchange
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: If B,D are bases and b∈B\D, there exists c∈D\B for which both B−b+c and D−c+b are bases.

entries.title: Weighted matroid greedy optimization
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: Scanning elements in nonincreasing real weight and retaining an element whenever independence is preserved produces a maximum-weight basis.

entries.title: Contraction has an explicit rank certificate
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: For A⊆E, the function r_A(X)=r(A∪X)−r(A) on E\A is a matroid rank function. If B is a basis of A, then I is independent in the contraction exactly when B∪I is independent in the original matroid.

entries.title: Matchable subsets form a transversal matroid
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: In a bipartite graph with left ground set L, the subsets of L that can be matched injectively into the right part form a matroid.

entries.title: Forests form a graphic matroid
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: The acyclic edge subsets of a graph form a matroid.

entries.title: Rota's basis rearrangement
entries.section: 2. Matroid rank, exchange and concrete representations
entries.statement: Given n labelled disjoint bases B₁,…,B_n of a rank-n matroid, their union can be partitioned into n bases, each meeting each B_i exactly once. Repeated underlying vectors may be represented by distinct parallel labelled elements.

entries.title: Hall's theorem, including the equality split
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: A matching saturating L exists if and only if |N(S)|≥|S| for all S⊆L.

entries.title: Berge's augmenting-path criterion
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: A matching M has maximum size exactly when no path alternates between edges outside and inside M and has both endpoints unmatched by M.

entries.title: König's matching–cover equality
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: In a bipartite graph, the maximum matching size equals the minimum vertex-cover size.

entries.title: Regular bipartite graphs have perfect matchings
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
