entries.statement: A bipartite graph or multigraph with every vertex of degree d>0 has a perfect matching.

entries.title: Bipartite edge coloring uses exactly Δ colors
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: The edges of a bipartite multigraph of maximum degree Δ can be partitioned into Δ matchings; no fewer suffice when Δ>0.

entries.title: Hall's theorem with demands and capacities
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: For integer demands b_l≥0 and capacities c_r≥0, assigning b_l distinct units from each l to adjacent right vertices without exceeding c_r is possible exactly when Σ_{l∈S}b_l≤Σ_{r∈N(S)}c_r for every S⊆L. Multiple units may use the same original edge.

entries.title: The deficiency formula
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: Put d=max_{S⊆L}(|S|−|N(S)|). Then a maximum matching has size |L|−d.

entries.title: Doubly stochastic matrices decompose into permutations
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: Every nonnegative n×n real matrix with all row and column sums one is a convex combination of permutation matrices.

entries.title: Unique bipartite perfect matchings admit forced-edge peeling
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: A nonempty bipartite graph with a unique perfect matching has a left vertex of degree one. Recursively deleting its forced edge and endpoints characterizes uniqueness.

entries.title: odd Latin squares have transversals
entries.section: 3. Matching and assignment certificates
entries.statement: Every Latin square of odd order n has n cells meeting each row, each column and each symbol exactly once.

entries.title: Flow decomposes into paths and cycles
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: A nonnegative s–t flow with no edges into s or out of t is a nonnegative sum of s–t path flows and directed cycle flows. Integer flows admit integer coefficients. A nonnegative circulation decomposes into cycles.

entries.title: Residual reachability certifies maximum flow
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: A feasible s–t flow is maximum if and only if its residual graph has no positive-capacity s–t path.

entries.title: Integral max-flow/min-cut
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: With integer capacities, a maximum integer flow exists and its value equals the minimum cut capacity.

entries.title: Directed vertex Menger theorem
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: For distinct vertices s,t with no edge s→t, the maximum number of internally vertex-disjoint directed s–t paths equals the minimum number of internal vertices whose removal separates s from t.

entries.title: Lower-bounded circulation criterion
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: For integer bounds 0≤l_e≤u_e, a circulation with l_e≤f_e≤u_e exists exactly when l(δ⁻S)≤u(δ⁺S) for every vertex set S.

entries.title: Directed incidence matrices are totally unimodular
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: Every square submatrix of an oriented vertex–edge incidence matrix has determinant 0, 1 or −1.

entries.title: Negative-cycle optimality for fixed-value flow
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: A feasible flow of fixed value and finite edge bounds has minimum linear cost exactly when its residual graph has no directed cycle of negative total cost.

entries.title: Tree metrics are sums of cut metrics
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: In a tree with nonnegative edge lengths, choose either component S_e of each edge deletion. Then d(x,y)=Σ_e l_e |1_{S_e}(x)−1_{S_e}(y)|. Thus, with positive lengths the tree metric embeds isometrically in a weighted ℓ¹ space; with zero lengths allowed the same holds for the metric quotient identifying points at zero distance.

entries.title: Prescribed outdegrees have a cut criterion
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: An undirected graph admits an orientation with specified integer outdegrees d(v)≥0 exactly when Σ_v d(v)=|E| and Σ_{v∈S}d(v)≥|E(S)| for every S⊆V.

entries.title: five even subgraphs double-cover edges
entries.section: 4. Flows, cuts, orientation and transport
entries.statement: Every bridgeless graph has five, possibly empty or disconnected, even-degree spanning subgraphs such that each edge occurs in exactly two of them. “Even subgraph” does not mean a single simple cycle.

entries.title: Three equivalent tree certificates
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: For a nonempty graph on n vertices, being connected and acyclic, having a unique simple path between every pair, and being connected with n−1 edges are equivalent.

entries.title: Fundamental cycles form a cycle-space basis
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: Over F₂, the even-degree edge subsets of a graph with n vertices, m edges and c components form a vector space of dimension m−n+c. For any spanning forest, the fundamental cycles of its nonforest edges are a basis.

entries.title: Cut and cycle spaces are orthogonal complements
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: In F₂^E, the cut space is the orthogonal complement of the even-degree cycle space. Its dimension is n−c.

entries.title: Euler tours from parity
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: A graph with at least one edge has a closed trail using every edge once exactly when all nonisolated vertices lie in one component and all degrees are even.

entries.title: Every tree has a balanced separator vertex
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: A tree on n≥1 vertices has a vertex whose deletion leaves components of size at most n/2.

entries.title: Diameter determines the radius of a tree
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: A tree of diameter D has radius ⌈D/2⌉, attained by either middle vertex of a diametral path.

entries.title: Prüfer coding and Cayley's count
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: Labelled trees on {1,…,n}, n≥2, correspond bijectively to words of length n−2 over these labels; consequently there are n^{n−2} trees.

entries.title: The matrix-tree determinant
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: For a connected graph, deleting any row and corresponding column of its Laplacian gives a determinant equal to its number of spanning trees.

entries.title: Degeneracy yields a forest decomposition
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: If every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree at most k, the edge set can be partitioned into k forests.

entries.title: every tree is graceful
entries.section: 5. Trees, cycle spaces and structural decompositions
entries.statement: Every tree with m edges admits a bijective vertex labeling by {0,…,m} for which its edge absolute differences are {1,…,m}.

entries.title: Mantel's triangle-free bound
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: A triangle-free graph on n vertices has at most n²/4 edges.

entries.title: Motzkin–Straus weighted clique bound
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: If a nonempty graph has clique number at most r≥1 and x_v≥0 with Σ_v x_v=1, then Σ_{uv∈E}x_u x_v≤(r−1)/(2r).

entries.title: Caro–Wei independent-set bound
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: Every graph has an independent set of size at least Σ_v 1/(d(v)+1).

entries.title: A quantitative triangle supersaturation bound
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: A graph on n>0 vertices with e edges has at least e(4e−n²)/(3n) triangles. A negative right side is merely a vacuous lower bound.

entries.title: A K₂,t incidence bound
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: For n≥1, if no two distinct vertices have t common neighbors, where t≥1, then e≤(n/4)[1+√(1+4(t−1)(n−1))].

entries.title: Dependent random choice with explicit parameters
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: In a bipartite graph with |A|=N>0, |B|=M>0 and average degree d on A, for positive integers t,r,m there is U⊆A of size at least N(d/M)^t−binom(N,r)(m/M)^t such that every r-subset of U has at least m common neighbors in B.

entries.title: Erdős–Szekeres monotone subsequences
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: For positive integers r,s, any sequence of rs+1 distinct real numbers has an increasing subsequence of length r+1 or a decreasing subsequence of length s+1.

entries.title: The binomial Ramsey bound
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: Every graph with at least binom(s+t−2,s−1) vertices contains a clique of size s or an independent set of size t, for s,t≥1.

entries.title: Packing supplies a hitting-set certificate
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: In an r-uniform hypergraph with r≥1, if ν is the largest disjoint-edge packing and τ the smallest vertex set meeting every edge, then ν≤τ≤rν.

entries.title: Tuza's factor two
entries.section: 6. Extremal graph and incidence tools
entries.statement: In every graph, the minimum number τ of edges meeting all triangles is at most twice the maximum number ν of edge-disjoint triangles.

entries.title: The LYM inequality for antichains
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: If F⊆2^[n] contains no two distinct comparable sets, then Σ_{A∈F}1/binom(n,|A|)≤1.

entries.title: Bollobás's set-pairs inequality
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: Suppose finite pairs (A_i,B_i) satisfy A_i∩B_i=∅ and A_i∩B_j≠∅ for all distinct i,j. Then Σ_i 1/binom(|A_i|+|B_i|,|A_i|)≤1.

entries.title: Sauer–Shelah counting
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: If F⊆2^[n] shatters no set larger than d≥0, then |F|≤Σ_{i=0}^{min(d,n)}binom(n,i). Shattering Y means every subset of Y occurs as A∩Y for some A∈F.

entries.title: Down-compression preserves size without creating shattered sets
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: At coordinate i, replace A containing i by A−i only when A−i is absent. This preserves family size and creates no new shattered set. Repeated coordinate compressions eventually produce a downset of the same size and no larger VC dimension.

entries.title: The factorial sunflower bound
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: For integers k≥1,r≥2, a family of distinct k-sets of size greater than k!(r−1)^k contains r sets whose pairwise intersections all equal one common core.

entries.title: Erdős–Ko–Rado via cyclic intervals
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: If n≥2k≥2 and an intersecting family F consists of k-subsets of [n], then |F|≤binom(n−1,k−1).

entries.title: Dilworth's chain decomposition
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: A finite poset's largest antichain size equals the least number of chains partitioning its elements.

entries.title: Mirsky's antichain decomposition
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: A finite poset of maximum chain size h can be partitioned into h antichains, and fewer are impossible.

entries.title: Harris positive correlation
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: For independent Bernoulli coordinates and increasing real functions f,g on their finite product cube, E(fg)≥Ef·Eg.

entries.title: a sharp inertia certificate for every downset
entries.section: 7. Set families, compression and order
entries.statement: Let D⊆2^[n] be a downset containing a nonempty set, and s=max_i |{A∈D:i∈A}|. There exists a real symmetric matrix M indexed by D, with M_AB=0 whenever A∩B≠∅, having exactly s nonnegative eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity. Negative and zero entries on allowed disjoint pairs are permitted; the empty-set diagonal is allowed.

entries.title: Root counting over a field
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: A nonzero univariate polynomial of degree d over a field has at most d distinct roots.

entries.title: Lagrange interpolation with its leading coefficient
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: For distinct field elements S, |S|=t+1, every polynomial of degree at most t satisfies P(X)=Σ_{a∈S}P(a)∏_{b∈S−a}(X−b)/(a−b). In particular [X^t]P=Σ_{a∈S}P(a)/∏_{b≠a}(a−b).

entries.title: Product-grid unisolvence
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: Let nonempty finite subsets S_i of a field be given. A multivariate polynomial with individual degree in X_i less than |S_i| that vanishes on ∏S_i is the zero polynomial.

entries.title: Coefficient formula and combinatorial Nullstellensatz
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: If deg P≤Σ_i t_i and |S_i|=t_i+1, then [∏X_i^{t_i}]P=Σ_{x∈∏S_i}P(x)/∏_i∏_{a∈S_i−x_i}(x_i−a). Thus a nonzero indicated coefficient forces a nonzero grid evaluation.

entries.title: Schwartz–Zippel identity testing
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: For a nonzero polynomial P of total degree d and independent uniform variables in a nonempty field subset S of size q, Pr(P=0)≤d/q.

entries.title: Minimum support on a product grid
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: If P≠0 has individual degrees at most d_i<|S_i|, then it is nonzero at at least ∏_i(|S_i|−d_i) grid points.

entries.title: Chevalley–Warning divisibility
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: For polynomials f₁,…,f_r over F_p with Σ_j deg f_j<n, the number of their common zeros in F_p^n is divisible by p. Zero polynomials may be omitted.

entries.title: Hyperplanes cannot cheaply cover a punctured grid
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: Let nonempty field subsets S_i and a distinguished x*∈∏S_i be given. If affine hyperplanes cover every grid point except x* and none contains x*, their number is at least Σ_i(|S_i|−1).

entries.title: Prime-order Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: Among any 2p−1 integers, p prime, there are p whose sum is divisible by p.

entries.title: Alon–Tarsi Latin parity
entries.section: 8. Polynomial grids and finite-field existence
entries.statement: For every positive even n, the signed sum over all Latin squares of order n is nonzero, where a square's sign is the product of the signs of all its row permutations and all its column permutations, using fixed ordered row, column and symbol labels.

entries.title: Möbius inversion on a finite poset
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: For a finite poset P define μ(x,x)=1 and, for x<y, μ(x,y)=−Σ_{x<z≤y}μ(z,y). If f(x)=Σ_{y≤x}g(y), then g(x)=Σ_{y≤x}μ(y,x)f(y). These two transformations are inverse over any commutative coefficient ring.

entries.title: Cauchy–Frobenius orbit counting
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: If a finite group G acts on a finite set X, the number of orbits is |G|⁻¹Σ_{g∈G}|Fix(g)|.

entries.title: Pólya's weighted cycle-index formula
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: Let a finite group G permute a finite position set Ω and let colors be 1,…,k with k≥1. For each orbit O of colorings c:Ω→{1,…,k}, assign its invariant monomial w(O)=∏_{u∈Ω}t_{c(u)}. Then Σ_O w(O)=|G|⁻¹Σ_{g∈G}∏_{cycles C of g}(Σ_{a=1}^k t_a^{|C|}), as a polynomial with rational coefficients.

entries.title: Incidence automorphisms are determined by their point action
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: If blocks are actual subsets of the point set, every incidence-preserving pair of point and block permutations is uniquely determined by its point permutation. A point permutation extends exactly when it permutes the block family.

entries.title: Necessary orders of Hadamard matrices
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: If an n×n matrix H with entries ±1 satisfies HHᵀ=nI and n>0, then n=1, n=2, or 4 divides n.

entries.title: Kronecker multiplication constructs Hadamard matrices
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: If H and K are Hadamard matrices of orders m and n, then H⊗K is Hadamard of order mn. In particular such matrices exist for every order 2^a, a≥0.

entries.title: Finite Fourier orthogonality, inversion and Parseval
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: On G=F_p^d, define χ_γ(x)=exp(2πi γ·x/p) and f̂(γ)=|G|⁻¹Σ_x f(x)overline(χ_γ(x)). Then the characters are an orthonormal basis under the uniform inner product; f(x)=Σ_γ f̂(γ)χ_γ(x) and Σ_γ|f̂(γ)|²=|G|⁻¹Σ_x|f(x)|².

entries.title: Biregular expander mixing with specified norm
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement:
For a bipartite incidence matrix M with row degree a and column degree b, let σ be the operator norm of M on the zero-sum subspace of R^R into R^L. Then for S⊆L,T⊆R,

|e(S,T)−a|S||T|/|R||≤σ√(|S|(1−|S|/|L|)|T|(1−|T|/|R|)), assuming both parts are nonempty.

entries.title: The binary Plotkin bound
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: A binary code of length n with M≥1 distinct words and minimum Hamming distance δ>n/2 satisfies M≤⌊2δ/(2δ−n)⌋.

entries.title: all admissible Hadamard orders
entries.section: 9. Enumeration, incidence symmetries and spectral counting
entries.statement: For every positive integer m there is a Hadamard matrix of order 4m.

entries.title: Cauchy–Davenport in prime order
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: For nonempty A,B⊆F_p, |A+B|≥min(p,|A|+|B|−1).

entries.title: Ordered sumsets have linear growth
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: For nonempty finite subsets A,B of R, |A+B|≥|A|+|B|−1.

entries.title: Ruzsa's triangle inequality
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: Nonempty finite additive sets satisfy |A−C||B|≤|A−B||B−C|.

entries.title: Ruzsa's covering lemma
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: If |A+B|≤K|B| with B nonempty, there is X⊆A, |X|≤K, such that A⊆X+(B−B).

entries.title: Additive energy and its maximal case
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: For finite nonempty A, E(A)=#{(a,b,c,d)∈A⁴:a+b=c+d} satisfies |A|⁴/|A+A|≤E(A)≤|A|³. Equality in the upper bound holds exactly when A is a coset of a finite subgroup.

entries.title: Petridis growth lemma and iterated sumsets
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: Choose nonempty X⊆A minimizing K=|X+B|/|X|. Then |X+B+C|≤K|X+C| for every finite nonempty C, and |X+kB|≤K^k|X| for all k≥0.

entries.title: Bogolyubov's subspace certificate
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: If A⊆F_p^d has density α>0, then 2A−2A contains a linear subspace of codimension at most ⌈2/α²⌉.

entries.title: Schur's finite monochromatic equation
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: Define m₁=3 and m_r=r(m_{r−1}−1)+2 for r≥2. Every coloring of {1,…,m_r−1} with r colors has same-colored positive integers x,y,z with x+y=z; x=y is allowed.

entries.title: A zero-sum subsequence in an elementary abelian group
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: Every sequence of d(p−1)+1 vectors in F_p^d has a nonempty subsequence summing to zero. Repetitions are allowed and subsequence means a subset of positions.

entries.title: Erdős–Turán additive bases
entries.section: 10. Additive structure, covering and zero sums
entries.statement: If A⊆N₀ and every sufficiently large integer is a sum of two elements of A, then r_A(n)=#{(a,b)∈A²:a≤b, a+b=n} is unbounded as n→∞, meaning limsup r_A(n)=∞.

entries.title: an exact curvature identity
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
For every real t,
\[
F''(t)=\frac12\sum_{i,j}p_t(i)p_t(j)(x_i-x_j)^2.
\]
Consequently F is convex, and strictly convex precisely when the x_i are not all equal.

entries.title: differentiation of a tilted observable
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
For any fixed real g_i,
\[
\frac d{dt}E_tg=\operatorname{Cov}_t(g,x)
 =\frac12\sum_{i,j}p_t(i)p_t(j)(g_i-g_j)(x_i-x_j).
\]
If g_i=h(x_i) for a nondecreasing h, E_tg is nondecreasing.

entries.title: a dimension-free variance bound
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement: If a≤x_i≤b, then 0≤F''(t)≤(b-a)²/4 for every t.

entries.title: the bounded-range exponential estimate
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
If x_i∈[a,b] and μ=sum p_ix_i, then for every real t,
\[
\sum_i p_i e^{t(x_i-\mu)}\le e^{t^2(b-a)^2/8}.
\]

entries.title: a variance-sensitive exponential estimate
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
If Y has finite distribution, EY=0, |Y|≤b with b>0, and EY²=σ², then for 0≤t<3/b,
\[
\log E e^{tY}\le\frac{\sigma^2t^2}{2(1-bt/3)}.
\]

entries.title: a finite Chernoff certificate
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
For t≥0 and any real u,
\[
\sum_{x_i\ge u}p_i\le e^{F(t)-tu}.
\]
Every explicit t thus gives a sufficient upper bound on the upper tail.

entries.title: the finite entropy variational formula
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
With 0 log 0=0 and KL(q||p)=sum q_i log(q_i/p_i),
\[
F(t)=\max_{q_i\ge0,\,\sum q_i=1}\{t\sum_iq_ix_i-\mathrm{KL}(q\Vert p)\},
\]
with unique maximizer q=p_t.

entries.title: total variation is controlled by entropy
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
For a probability vector q and strictly positive p,
\[
\frac12\sum_i|q_i-p_i|\le\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}(q\Vert p)/2}.
\]

entries.title: entropy-stable expectations
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
If g_i∈[a,b], then
\[
|E_qg-E_pg|\le(b-a)\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}(q\Vert p)/2}.
\]

entries.title: concentration of independent finite sums
entries.section: 1. Finite exponential families and quantitative convexity
entries.statement:
Let independent finite-valued X_j satisfy X_j∈[a_j,b_j], and set V=sum_j(b_j-a_j)². If V>0 and u>0,
\[
\Pr\{\sum_j(X_j-EX_j)\ge u\}\le e^{-2u^2/V}.
\]

entries.title: existence and uniqueness of a positive moment root
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement: If A=sum a_i<1, there is exactly one τ>0 with Z(τ)=1.

entries.title: explicit support-only root brackets
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement:
Under D011, with b_min=min b_i and b_max=max b_i,
\[
\frac{\log(1/A)}{b_{\max}}\le\tau\le\frac{\log(1/A)}{b_{\min}}.
\]

entries.title: sensitivity to a coefficient perturbation
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement:
Suppose a_i(s)>0 are C¹ near s_0, sum a_i(s)<1 there, and the rates are fixed. The positive root τ(s) is C¹ and
\[
\tau'(s)=-\frac{\sum_i a_i'(s)e^{b_i\tau(s)}}{\sum_i a_i(s)b_ie^{b_i\tau(s)}}.
\]

entries.title: the inverse moment is increasing and concave
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement: For every B>0 there is a unique real T(B) with Z(T(B))=B. It satisfies T'(B)=1/Z'(T(B))>0 and T''(B)=-Z''(T(B))/Z'(T(B))³<0.

entries.title: root stability from a slope certificate
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement: Suppose continuous Z,W have roots Z(τ)=W(σ)=1 in an interval J, Z is differentiable there with Z'≥m>0, and |Z-W|≤ε on J. Then |τ-σ|≤ε/m.

entries.title: error propagation through a finite exponential sum
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement:
If x_i,y_i≤M_i and a_i,\widetilde a_i are real, then
\[
|\sum a_ie^{x_i}-\sum\widetilde a_ie^{y_i}|
\le\sum_i e^{M_i}(|a_i-\widetilde a_i|+|\widetilde a_i|\,|x_i-y_i|).
\]

entries.title: amortizing a positive residue strictly improves a root
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement: Let P,Q be continuous on an interval J, Q>0 there. Suppose every f_T=P+Q/T, for T>0 under consideration, is strictly increasing on J and has a root τ_T at level one. If S<T, then τ_S<τ_T.

entries.title: the first two amortization corrections
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement:
Let P,Q be C³ near t_0, P(t_0)=1 and p=P'(t_0)>0. The nearby solution of P(t)+uQ(t)=1 has expansion
\[
t=t_0-\frac{Q(t_0)}p u+
\left(\frac{Q'(t_0)Q(t_0)}{p^2}-\frac{P''(t_0)Q(t_0)^2}{2p^3}\right)u^2+O(u^3).
\]

entries.title: coupling ordered rates orders the roots
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement: Fix positive a_i with sum a_i<1. If b_i≥c_i>0, then the roots τ_b,τ_c of sum a_i e^{b_it}=1 and sum a_i e^{c_it}=1 obey τ_b≤τ_c. If at least one inequality is strict, so is the root inequality.

entries.title: rational logarithm and exponential enclosures
entries.section: 2. Strict roots, perturbations, and finite certificates
entries.statement:
For rational r≥1 put z=(r-1)/(r+1). For N≥1,
\[
0\le\log r-2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{z^{2j+1}}{2j+1}
\le\frac{2z^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-z^2)}.
\]
For rational x≥0 and integer m≥0 with x<m+2,
\[
0\le e^x-\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{x^k}{k!}
\le\frac{x^{m+1}}{(m+1)!}\frac1{1-x/(m+2)}.
\]

entries.title: a reverse averaging move decreases concave cost
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: Let f be concave on [0,U]. If 0≤d≤x≤y and y+d≤U, then f(x-d)+f(y+d)≤f(x)+f(y).

entries.title: majorization gives a sufficient concave-cost comparison
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: Let decreasing real vectors x,y of length n lie in an interval, have equal sum, and satisfy sum_{i≤k}x_i≥sum_{i≤k}y_i for every k. For every concave f on that interval, sum f(x_i)≤sum f(y_i).

entries.title: exact minimum under one mass constraint and a cap
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: For x∈[0,U]^n, U>0, with sum x_i=M, a minimum of sum f(x_i), for concave f, is attained by k=floor(M/U) entries U, at most one entry r=M-kU∈(0,U), and all remaining entries zero.

entries.title: a concave minimum has few interior coordinates
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: Let P={x∈[l,u]^n:Ax=b} be nonempty, with l<u and rank A=k. Every continuous concave function on P has a minimizer with at most k coordinates strictly between their bounds.

entries.title: the complementary maximum is uniform
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: If f is concave on an interval and x_1,...,x_n lie there, n≥1, then sum f(x_i)≤n f((sum x_i)/n). For strictly concave f, equality holds exactly when all coordinates are equal.

entries.title: curvature pays a quantitative majorization margin
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement:
Suppose f is C² on [l,u], f''≤-c with c≥0, and x majorizes y as in D022. Then
\[
\sum f(y_i)-\sum f(x_i)\ge\frac c2\left(\sum x_i^2-\sum y_i^2\right).
\]

entries.title: a finite convex-order test
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: Let X,Y have finite real distributions and equal means. Then Eφ(X)≤Eφ(Y) for every convex φ if and only if E(X-t)_+≤E(Y-t)_+ for every real t. It suffices to check t in the union of their supports.

entries.title: fractional powers are mixtures of capped linear functions
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement:
For 0<p<1 and x≥0,
\[
x^p=p(1-p)\int_0^\infty\min(x,t)t^{p-2}\,dt.
\]
Consequently equal-mean convex order X≤cxY implies EX^p≥EY^p for nonnegative finite X,Y.

entries.title: concave sums have an ordered assignment optimum
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement: Let a_1≤...≤a_n and b_1≤...≤b_n, with all relevant sums in the domain of a concave f. Among permutations π, sum_i f(a_i+b_{π(i)}) is minimized by the same order and maximized by reverse order.

entries.title: a global fractional-power perturbation bound
entries.section: 3. Concavity, transport, and extremal finite profiles
entries.statement:
If 0<p≤1 and x,y∈[0,∞)^n, n≥1, then
\[
|\sum x_i^p-\sum y_i^p|\le\sum|x_i-y_i|^p
\le n^{1-p}(\sum|x_i-y_i|)^p.
\]

entries.title: the sharp norm of a scalar shear
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement:
On H⊕H for a nonzero finite-dimensional Hilbert space H, let S_a(x,y)=(x+ay,y), a≥0. Then
\[
\|S_a\|=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+4}+a}{2}.
\]

entries.title: tensor products multiply Hilbert operator norms
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: For finite-dimensional Hilbert operators A,B, ||A⊗B||=||A||·||B||.

entries.title: direct-sum norm accounting needs no independence
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: For a finite nonempty family T_i:H_i→K_i, the operator ⊕T_i on Hilbert direct sums has norm max_i||T_i||.

entries.title: growth is charged per persistent block
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement:
Suppose A_s=⊕_i A_{s,i} are composable operators on a fixed Hilbert block decomposition and ||A_{s,i}||≤a_{s,i}≥0. Then
\[
\|A_{m-1}\cdots A_0x\|^2\le
\sum_i\left(\prod_{s<m}a_{s,i}\right)^2\|x_i\|^2.
\]
In particular the product norm is at most max_i product_s a_{s,i}.

entries.title: a weighted Schur test for operator blocks
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: Let T=(T_ij), c_ij≥||T_ij||. If positive u_i,v_j and R,C≥0 satisfy sum_j c_ij v_j≤R u_i and sum_i c_ij u_i≤C v_j, then ||T||≤sqrt(RC).

entries.title: a constructive positive weight for a stable nonnegative matrix
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: For a positive-size finite square entrywise nonnegative matrix C with spectral radius ρ(C)<1, w=(I-C)^(-1)1 is well-defined, w_i≥1, and Cw=w-1. Thus ||Cx||_w≤r||x||_w for ||x||_w=max_i|x_i|/w_i and r=max_i(1-1/w_i)<1.

entries.title: a forced nonnegative recurrence has a uniform bound
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement:
If u_n,d_n are nonnegative vectors, u_{n+1}≤Cu_n+d_n coordinatewise, C≥0, Cw≤rw for w>0 and 0≤r<1, and ||d_n||_w≤D, then
\[
\|u_n\|_w\le r^n\|u_0\|_w+D\frac{1-r^n}{1-r}.
\]

entries.title: acyclic coupling has a finite path certificate
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: If C is an entrywise nonnegative strictly upper triangular n×n matrix, then (I-C)^(-1)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1}C^k. Each inverse entry is the sum of products of edge weights over all directed paths between the corresponding vertices, including the empty path on the diagonal.

entries.title: local prefix norms compose with boundary norms
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: Let complete boundary states be x_s=A_{s-1}...A_0x_0 with ||x_s||≤B_s||x_0||. Suppose each observable intermediate state during step s is P_{s,r}x_s with ||P_{s,r}||≤M_s. Then every such observable has norm at most (max_s M_s B_s)||x_0||.

entries.title: coherent isometric gauges preserve block growth bounds
entries.section: 4. Block operators and complete-boundary energy
entries.statement: Let U_s be unitary identifications and let A_s=U_{s+1}D_sU_s^(-1), where every D_s uses one fixed block decomposition. Then ||A_{m-1}...A_0||=||D_{m-1}...D_0||, so D034 applies.

entries.title: discrete variation of constants
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement:
If E_s,b_s≥0, a_s≥0 and E_{s+1}≤(1+a_s)E_s+b_s, then
\[
E_n\le E_0\prod_{s<n}(1+a_s)+\sum_{j<n}b_j\prod_{j<s<n}(1+a_s)
\le E_0e^{\sum a_s}+\sum_{j<n}b_je^{\sum_{j<s<n}a_s}.
\]

entries.title: adjustable quadratic splitting
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement:
In a Hilbert space, for ε>0,
\[
\|x+y\|^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\|x\|^2+(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\|y\|^2.
\]
If x,y are nonzero, minimizing the right side over ε gives (||x||+||y||)².

entries.title: a common quadratic metric controls arbitrary switching
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement:
Let Q>0 and r≥0, and suppose every operator in a family satisfies A*QA≤r²Q. Every length-n product P of operators from that family obeys
\[
\|P\|\le\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(Q)/\lambda_{\min}(Q)}\,r^n.
\]

entries.title: repeated one-direction shears grow only linearly in their parameter
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement:
For nonzero Hilbert spaces H,K and A:K→H, let S_A(x,y)=(x+Ay,y). For every integer n≥0,
\[
S_A^n(x,y)=(x+nAy,y),\qquad
\|S_A^n\|=\frac{\sqrt{n^2\|A\|^2+4}+n\|A\|}{2}.
\]

entries.title: a paired shear has an explicit invariant metric
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement:
For real |a|<2, set
\[
T=\begin{pmatrix}1-a^2&a\\-a&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&-a/2\\-a/2&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then T^TQT=Q and, for every integer n, ||T^n||≤sqrt((1+|a|/2)/(1-|a|/2)).

entries.title: the Hermitian part controls an exponential
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement: For any square complex matrix A, put μ=λ_max((A+A*)/2). Then ||e^{tA}||≤e^{tμ} for t≥0.

entries.title: a stable matrix admits a constructive quadratic metric
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement: If ρ(A)<1, the series Q=sum_{k≥0}(A*)^k A^k converges, Q≥I, and Q-A*QA=I. Consequently A is a strict contraction in its Q norm.

entries.title: a quadratic stability margin survives perturbations
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement: Suppose Q>0, ||A||_Q≤r, and ||E||≤ε in Euclidean norm. Then ||A+E||_Q≤r+ε sqrt(κ(Q)). In particular this is a contraction when ε<(1-r)/sqrt(κ(Q)).

entries.title: finite observability gives exact and stable recovery
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement: Let O:x↦(Cx,CAx,...,CA^{m-1}x) and G=O*O. Then G>0 if and only if the only x with CA^kx=0 for 0≤k<m is zero. If G≥γI>0, the map G^{-1}O* recovers x from Ox and has norm at most γ^{-1/2}.

entries.title: every finite-group representation can be isometrized
entries.section: 5. Lyapunov metrics, switching, and exact cancellation
entries.statement: For a representation ρ of a finite group by invertible complex matrices, define Q=|G|^{-1}sum_g ρ(g)*ρ(g). Then Q>0 and ρ(h)*Qρ(h)=Q. If M=max_g||ρ(g)||, then M^{-2}I≤Q≤M²I.

entries.title: the weighted Hankel factorization
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: Over any commutative ring, H_M=V^T diag(w)V.

entries.title: positive nodes weights give the exact Hankel rank
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: If the λ_i are distinct real numbers, w_i>0, and M≥N, then H_M is positive semidefinite of rank N.

entries.title: repeated nodes must first be aggregated
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: Over a field, aggregate equal nodes by adding their weights and discard nodes with aggregate weight zero. If q distinct nodes remain, then rank H_M=q whenever M≥q.

entries.title: the annihilating polynomial is recovered from finitely many moments
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: For N distinct real nodes and positive weights, the monic polynomial P(t)=product_i(t-λ_i) is the unique monic degree-N polynomial satisfying L(t^jP)=0 for 0≤j<N, where L(t^k)=m_k.

entries.title: an annihilator supplies a recurrence at every later index
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: If P(t)=sum_{j=0}^N c_jt^j vanishes at every λ_i, then sum_{j=0}^N c_jm_{k+j}=0 for every integer k≥0.

entries.title: the recurrence order counts the surviving nodes
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: If distinct nodes have nonzero weights over a field, the smallest degree of a monic polynomial giving the recurrence of D055 for every k≥0 is N.

entries.title: the generating function records reciprocal poles
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement:
As a formal power series,
\[
\sum_{k\ge0}m_kz^k=\sum_i\frac{w_i}{1-\lambda_i z}.
\]
If all nodes and weights are nonzero and nodes are distinct, the reduced denominator has degree N and roots 1/λ_i.

entries.title: 2N moments uniquely recover an N-atom positive measure
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: The moments m_0,...,m_{2N-1} of N distinct real nodes with positive weights determine those nodes and weights uniquely, up to permutation, among positive representations with at most N atoms.

entries.title: a flat positive Hankel extension gives a representing measure
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement: Let N≥1 and real m_0,...,m_{2N} satisfy H_N>0, H_{N+1}≥0 and rank H_{N+1}=N. Then there is a unique positive Borel representing measure for these moments; it has exactly N real atoms.

entries.title: separated nodes give an explicit weight-recovery bound
entries.section: 6. Hankel structure and exact finite recovery
entries.statement:
Let real nodes satisfy |λ_i|≤R and |λ_i-λ_j|≥δ>0 for i≠j. If fixed-node weights w,\widetilde w have first N moment vectors m,\widetilde m, then
\[
\|w-\widetilde w\|_\infty\le
\left(\frac{1+R}{\delta}\right)^{N-1}\|m-\widetilde m\|_\infty.
\]

entries.title: positivity supplies a Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement: Let L be a real linear functional on polynomials of degree at most 2d and suppose L(p²)≥0 for every p of degree at most d. Then |L(pq)|²≤L(p²)L(q²) for such p,q.

entries.title: positive odd-degree data have a Gaussian representation
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement: If real m_0,...,m_{2N-1}, N≥1, have H_N>0, there are N distinct real nodes and positive weights reproducing every given moment.

entries.title: a signed quadrature error is controlled by one even derivative
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
Let μ be a positive finite measure on [a,b], and let positive nodes-and-weights quadrature with N distinct nodes λ_i∈[a,b] be exact for polynomials of degree at most 2N-1. Put P(t)=product_i(t-λ_i). For f∈C^{2N}[a,b],
\[
|\int f\,d\mu-\sum_iw_if(\lambda_i)|
\le\frac{\|f^{(2N)}\|_\infty}{(2N)!}\int P(t)^2\,d\mu(t).
\]
If f^{(2N)}≥0 the error on the left before absolute value is nonnegative.

entries.title: the Christoffel minimizer is explicit
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
Let H_N>0 be the Gram matrix of a polynomial functional L on degrees below N, and v(x)=(1,x,...,x^{N-1})^T. Among polynomials p of degree below N satisfying p(x)=1,
\[
\min L(p^2)=\frac1{v(x)^TH_N^{-1}v(x)}.
\]
The minimizing coefficient vector is H_N^{-1}v/(v^TH_N^{-1}v).

entries.title: a moment matrix bounds every atom weight
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement: In D064, if L is represented by a positive measure with an atom of weight w at x, then w≤1/(v(x)^TH_N^{-1}v(x)). If the measure has exactly N distinct atoms, equality holds at each atom.

entries.title: Gaussian resolvents have an exact positive error formula
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
Under D063, for real z>b,
\[
\int\frac{d\mu(x)}{z-x}-\sum_i\frac{w_i}{z-\lambda_i}
=\frac1{P(z)^2}\int\frac{P(x)^2}{z-x}\,d\mu(x)\ge0.
\]

entries.title: truncated moments control an exterior resolvent
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
Suppose positive finite measures μ,ν are supported in [-R,R], have masses M_μ,M_ν, and moment differences Δm_k. For z>R and integer K≥0,
\[
|S_\mu(z)-S_\nu(z)|\le\sum_{k=0}^K\frac{|\Delta m_k|}{z^{k+1}}
+\frac{(M_\mu+M_\nu)R^{K+1}}{z^{K+1}(z-R)},
\quad S_\mu(z)=\int(z-x)^{-1}d\mu.
\]

entries.title: compression gives a variational inverse bound
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
Let M>0, b be a vector, and V have full column rank. Then
\[
b^*V(V^*MV)^{-1}V^*b\le b^*M^{-1}b.
\]

entries.title: the compression error is exactly an energy projection error
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
In D068, x_*=M^{-1}b and x_V=V(V*MV)^{-1}V*b satisfy
\[
b^*M^{-1}b-b^*x_V=\|x_*-x_V\|_M^2.
\]
Moreover x_V minimizes this error over range V, and if M≥aI>0 with residual r=b-Mx_V, then ||x_*-x_V||_M≤||r||/sqrt(a).

entries.title: a Krylov subspace gives an exponential energy-error bound
entries.section: 7. Positive functionals, quadrature, and resolvent recovery
entries.statement:
Let aI≤M≤bI, 0<a≤b, and let x_m be the energy projection of M^{-1}v onto span(v,Mv,...,M^{m-1}v), m≥1. With κ=b/a,
\[
\|M^{-1}v-x_m\|_M^2\le4\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^{2m}\|M^{-1}v\|_M^2.
\]

entries.title: an approximate intertwiner has a controlled power defect
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement:
For square A,B of compatible sizes and rectangular X, if ||AX-XB||≤ε, then
\[
\|A^nX-XB^n\|\le\varepsilon\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\|A\|^{n-1-k}\|B\|^k
\]
for n≥1.

entries.title: spectral separation makes a Sylvester equation coercive
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement: If A,B are normal and |λ-μ|≥δ>0 for every λ∈spec A, μ∈spec B, then ||X||_F≤δ^{-1}||AX-XB||_F.

entries.title: separated spectral clusters admit a nearby block-respecting map
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement:
Let normal A,B have mutually orthogonal spectral-cluster projections P_i,Q_i summing to identity. Suppose spectra of A on P_i and B on Q_j are δ-separated whenever i≠j. Then X_0=sum_iP_iXQ_i satisfies
\[
\|X-X_0\|_F\le\delta^{-1}\|AX-XB\|_F.
\]

entries.title: the rectangular polar factor is the closest isometry
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement:
Let X:C^m→C^n, n≥m≥1, satisfy ||X*X-I||≤η<1. Then X has full column rank and U=X(X*X)^(-1/2) is an isometry. If σ_1,...,σ_m>0 are its singular values, then among all isometries V:C^m→C^n,
\[
\min_V\|X-V\|=\max_j|\sigma_j-1|,\qquad
\min_V\|X-V\|_F^2=\sum_j(\sigma_j-1)^2.
\]
U attains both minima and uniquely attains the Frobenius minimum. Moreover ||X-U||≤η/(1+sqrt(1-η)). If n=m, U is unitary, X is invertible and ||X^(-1)||≤(1-η)^(-1/2).

entries.title: polar correction preserves an exact self-adjoint intertwiner
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement: If A,B are self-adjoint, X is invertible and AX=XB, then U=X(X*X)^{-1/2} is unitary and AU=UB.

entries.title: polar repair has a controlled covariance loss
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement: Suppose X is square, ||A||,||B||≤1, ||AX-XB||≤ε and X satisfies D074. Its unitary polar factor obeys ||AU-UB||≤ε+2η/(1+sqrt(1-η)).

entries.title: finite averaging constructs an exact nearby intertwiner
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement: For finite-group representations ρ,σ by invertible complex matrices and a compatible X, put X_0=|G|^{-1}sum_gρ(g)^{-1}Xσ(g). Then ρ(h)X_0=X_0σ(h). If all group defects ||ρ(g)X-Xσ(g)||≤ε and M=max_g||ρ(g)^{-1}||, then ||X-X_0||≤Mε. In equal dimensions X_0 is invertible whenever the least singular value of X exceeds Mε.

entries.title: a nearly invariant positive metric can be repaired
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement:
Let Q>0 and η=||Q^{-1/2}(A*QA-Q)Q^{-1/2}||<1. There is B with B*QB=Q and
\[
\|A-B\|\le\sqrt{\kappa(Q)}\frac\eta{1+\sqrt{1-\eta}}.
\]

entries.title: finite unitary averaging is a positive orthogonal projection
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement: If ρ is a finite-group unitary representation, E(X)=|G|^{-1}sum_gρ(g)Xρ(g)* is the Frobenius-orthogonal projection onto its commutant. It is unital, trace preserving, completely positive, and contractive in every unitarily invariant norm.

entries.title: commutator defects measure distance to the commutant
entries.section: 8. Intertwiners, polar repair, and finite symmetry
entries.statement:
With E from D079,
\[
\|X-E(X)\|_F^2=\frac1{2|G|}\sum_g\|X-\rho(g)X\rho(g)^*\|_F^2.
\]
In particular an average squared commutator defect at most ε² implies distance at most ε/sqrt 2.

entries.title: a matrix exponential is locally Lipschitz with an explicit bound
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement:
For square A,B and t≥0,
\[
\|e^{tA}-e^{tB}\|\le t\|A-B\|e^{t\max(\|A\|,\|B\|)}.
\]

entries.title: skew-adjoint evolution has no exponential perturbation loss
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement: If A*=-A and B*=-B, then ||e^{tA}-e^{tB}||≤t||A-B|| for t≥0.

entries.title: the Lie product has a commutator-controlled local error
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement:
For skew-adjoint A,B and t≥0,
\[
\|e^{t(A+B)}-e^{tA}e^{tB}\|\le\frac{t^2}{2}\|[A,B]\|.
\]

entries.title: repeated Lie splitting has an explicit global error
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins

entries.title: a direct local bound for symmetric splitting
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement:
Let M=||A||+||B||, h≥0 and S_h=e^{hA/2}e^{hB}e^{hA/2}. Then
\[
\|S_h-e^{h(A+B)}\|\le\frac{(hM)^3e^{hM}}3.
\]

entries.title: symmetric unitary splitting has second-order global accuracy
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement:
If A,B are skew-adjoint, M=||A||+||B||, t≥0, and n≥1, then
\[
\|S_{t/n}^n-e^{t(A+B)}\|\le\frac{t^3M^3e^{tM/n}}{3n^2}.
\]

entries.title: a finite Taylor polynomial has a certified matrix remainder
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement:
For m≥0,
\[
\left\|e^A-\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{A^k}{k!}\right\|
\le\frac{\|A\|^{m+1}e^{\|A\|}}{(m+1)!}.
\]

entries.title: log determinants have a spectral-floor stability bound
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement: If A,B are n×n positive definite Hermitian matrices with A,B≥aI>0, then |log det A-log det B|≤(n/a)||A-B||.

entries.title: diagonal dominance certifies a positive spectral floor
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement: For a Hermitian matrix A define a=min_i(A_ii-sum_{j≠i}|A_ij|) and b=max_i(A_ii+sum_{j≠i}|A_ij|). Then aI≤A≤bI. In particular a>0 is a sufficient positive-definiteness certificate.

entries.title: inverse reconstruction by a finite Neumann polynomial
entries.section: 9. Matrix functions and explicit approximation margins
entries.statement:
If α>0 and q=||I-αA||<1, then A is invertible and
\[
\left\|A^{-1}-\alpha\sum_{k=0}^m(I-\alpha A)^k\right\|
\le\frac{\alpha q^{m+1}}{1-q}.
\]
For aI≤A≤bI, 0<a≤b, the choice α=2/(a+b) gives q≤(b-a)/(b+a).

entries.title: generalized Vandermonde matrices are strictly positive
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: For r≥1, if 0<x_1<...<x_r and α_1<...<α_r are real, then det(x_i^{α_j})_{i,j=1}^r>0.

entries.title: positive moment sequences have strict ordered minors
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement:
If 0<λ_1<...<λ_N, w_i>0 and m_k=sum_iw_iλ_i^k, then for strictly increasing nonnegative integer lists r_1<...<r_q and c_1<...<c_q, q≤N,
\[
\det(m_{r_i+c_j})_{i,j=1}^q>0.
\]

entries.title: localizing matrices put recovered atoms in an interval
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: Given real m_0,...,m_{2N-1}, let H=(m_{i+j})_{i,j<N}>0 and X=(m_{i+j+1})_{i,j<N}. If aH≤X≤bH, then the N-node positive representation in D062 is supported in [a,b].

entries.title: finitely many odd moments certify reflection symmetry
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: Let d_1,...,d_N be distinct positive real numbers. A measure with respective weights u_i,v_i at d_i,-d_i is reflection invariant if its odd moments of orders 1,3,...,2N-1 vanish; the converse also holds.

entries.title: finitely many Laurent moments certify inversion symmetry
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: Let μ be a nonzero finite atomic positive measure on (0,∞), and let S be the union of its support and its reciprocal support, q=|S|. If m_r=m_{-r} for r=0,...,q-1, then μ is invariant under x↦1/x. The converse holds for every integer r.

entries.title: strict polynomial positivity eventually has positive Bernstein coefficients
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: Let p(t)=sum_{j=0}^d a_jt^j satisfy p≥ε>0 on [0,1]. For integers n≥max(1,2d) with n>d²sum_j|a_j|/ε, every degree-n Bernstein coefficient of p is positive.

entries.title: Bernstein degree elevation preserves certified bounds
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: If p=sum_{k=0}^n b_k B_{k,n}, its degree-(n+1) coefficients are c_0=b_0, c_{n+1}=b_n and c_k=(k/(n+1))b_{k-1}+(1-k/(n+1))b_k. Hence any common interval containing the b_k also contains every c_k.

entries.title: finite group convolution has a universal norm certificate
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: For a finite group G, Hilbert-valued functions f, and coefficients a_g, define T_af(h)=sum_g a_g f(hg). Then ||T_a||_{2→2}≤sum_g|a_g|. If a_g≥0, equality holds whenever the value space is nonzero.

entries.title: characters give an exact finite abelian norm test
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement: Let G be a product of finite cyclic groups. For T_a in D098 acting on complex scalar-valued functions, and each character χ, put α_χ=sum_g a_gχ(g). Then ||T_a||=max_χ|α_χ|. It is unitary exactly when every |α_χ|=1, and a contraction exactly when all are at most one.

entries.title: a lazy generating convolution has a quantitative mixing bound
entries.section: 10. Bridges between moments, positivity, and harmonic analysis
entries.statement:
In D099 let a be a symmetric probability vector, a_g=a_{g^{-1}}, with a_e>0 and support generating G. For nontrivial G set η=max_{χ≠1}|α_χ|. Then η<1, and for every mean-zero f,
\[
\|T_a^nf\|_2\le\eta^n\|f\|_2.
\]
Also (1/2)sum_g a_g||f(\cdot g)-f||_2²=〈f,(I-T_a)f〉≥(1-max_{χ≠1}α_χ)||f||_2².
